setting: The Aske Coast: a stretch of coast about a day's walk from north to south, between the sea in the east and bare mountains in the west. In the north a great forest reaches the shore; the palisaded timber town of Brandholm stands there. In the south lie reed beds, shallows and fishing streams; the open fishing town of Saltreach stands there. Between them, in the open middle lands, is the hamlet of Oathstone around a tall grey standing stone, where the two towns meet to trade. Deer graze the open land and wolves roam the woods. The seasons turn quickly; in winter nothing grows, nights are bitter, and food that is not cooked, smoked or stored spoils.

towns.name: Brandholm
towns.character: a palisaded timber town where the great northern forest meets the sea: hunters, trappers, carpenters, tanners and toolmakers; timber and hides are plentiful, fish and berries scarce
towns.ledger: The law of Brandholm, cut in the gate board: What a household hunts is the household's. The common store feeds the old, the young and the hurt first. Whoever takes from the common store without the Headwoman's word is shamed at the fire. The gates close at dark.

sheet.narrative: I have spent my life trying to keep Brandholm fed and its word worth something. My hands ache, and some mornings I have to sit before I can stand, but I still listen at the fire before I decide. I trust Maelis grudgingly, and I am fond of Aud; both know what an oath costs.
goals: Keep Brandholm from breaking the Oath
Leave the town steady enough to endure a change in leadership
Protect the young and hurt when stores run short
sheet.mood: Weary and watchful

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She is careful with her hands and with her promises; I hope the town hears her.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: son-in-law
relations.note: Quiet, useful, and steady; I am glad Sigrun has him beside her.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: She watches the hunters with bright eyes, and I would rather those eyes stayed bright.

relations.name: Bo
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: He still reaches for Liv whenever the wolves howl.

relations.name: Ragna
relations.label: sister
relations.note: We have told the same old winter in different ways for too long.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He speaks of feeding our own, but I fear what he would spend to prove it.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: ally
relations.note: Her tablets irritate me, but her care for the peace is plain.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: witness
relations.note: She stood at the stone when the words were spoken; I value her patience.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: oath-partner
relations.note: Her late husband and I spoke the same promise, though we carry different winters.

memories.gist: I was twenty when the Hunger Winter came. I remember the fear of empty stores and how quickly people learned to call their own hunger another household's fault.
At the stone, I swore with Sabeth's husband that there would be no blood between our towns and that we would trade. My voice shook less than my hands.
The last time Maelis read out a debt, I wanted to snap at her. Instead I listened, because the numbers were hers to keep and the peace was mine to protect.
I watched Brann's hunters come back talking as if the middle lands were theirs to take. I thought of the Oath and felt old in a way my bones could not explain.

stances.why: A promise made before witnesses is the only thing keeping old quarrels from becoming new blood.
We have hides and meat, but we cannot make everything we need alone.
A town that lets its weakest go cold has already begun to fail.
A hunt over the boundary could cost more than any trade debt.

sheet.narrative: I know the feel of a hide that will take a good seam and a cloak that will keep someone alive. Trade is not weakness; it is how we make up for what the land gives unevenly. I want the Oath kept, and I want Brandholm to learn enough to bargain without fear or bluster.
goals: Keep the Oath and widen trade
Learn to read and write from Maelis
Make Brandholm's leadership answer to more than a hunter's pride
sheet.mood: Determined, with a guarded patience

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She taught me that a spoken promise must survive a hungry season.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He steadies a room without needing to fill it with words.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: I admire her courage, though hunting is not the only worthy skill.

relations.name: Bo
relations.label: son
relations.note: He follows Liv everywhere, even when the wolves frighten him.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He hears every compromise as a defeat.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: teacher
relations.note: I respect her record and want her to teach me letters.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: trade-partner
relations.note: He counts every bundle, but he counts fairly enough.

relations.name: Inga
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She can speak plainly without turning every worry into a quarrel.

relations.name: Gudrun
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She makes my place in this family sound like something I stole.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: His work holds together better than most people's arguments.

relations.name: Ragna
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She keeps our old stories alive, though I wish she would leave more room for the south's telling.

relations.name: Vidar
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: He is fair-minded, and I value that he does not borrow his mother's quarrel with me.

relations.name: Egil
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: His hands make tools Brandholm could trade well, if we were less afraid of widening the bargain.

memories.gist: I remember the Oath day as a child: the adults stood so still at the stone that even we children stopped fidgeting.
After last winter's trade, I saw how much fish and nets mattered to our households. A cloak can be warm and still not fill a pot.
At a trade day, Maelis read the entries aloud and I found myself wanting to understand every mark on her tablet.
Gudrun and I once worked hides side by side without needing to talk. Now even a quiet room between us feels like an accusation.

stances.why: Without it, a trade road can become a path for revenge.
Both towns have things the other needs, and fear makes every winter harder.
A record lets us understand what we owe instead of treating every tally as an insult.
A leader should be judged by what her work and choices do for the town.

sheet.narrative: I would rather mend a beam than argue about who is strongest. A good joint holds because each piece is cut to fit, not because one piece shouts at the other. I have learned to notice when Ulf goes quiet; I do not always know how to ask him what is wrong.
goals: Keep the household sheltered and supplied
Support Sigrun without making every disagreement a fight
Be worthy of what Halvard taught me
sheet.mood: Quietly concerned

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She sees a path through trouble before most of us see the trouble.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She carries the town's weight even when her body asks her to put it down.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She wants to be like Siv; I hope she learns to choose her own measure.

relations.name: Bo
relations.label: son
relations.note: He is brave enough to follow Liv and honest enough to fear wolves.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: teacher
relations.note: His lessons were patient, and his tools still tell me when I have done poor work.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Since that winter he has gone quiet; I wish I knew how to reach him.

relations.name: Maren
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She brings more life into a room than I usually manage.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: hunt-leader
relations.note: I do not like how quickly his plans turn other people's homes into risks.

relations.name: Gudrun
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She knows her craft, but the old bitterness between her and Sigrun makes every family gathering feel like a board with a hidden crack.

memories.gist: Halvard showed me how to fit a door into a frame so it would still swing after the wood swelled in damp weather. I have used that lesson more times than I can count.
When Liv was small, she fell asleep against my shoulder while Sigrun worked late on a cloak. I stayed still until my arm went numb.
One winter Ulf stopped laughing at the fire. I noticed, but all I managed was to sit nearby and keep my hands busy.
I have watched Sigrun and Hekka disagree without either of them forgetting they are family. That is harder work than building a wall.

stances.why: A thing made carefully keeps serving people after an argument is forgotten.
Travel and trade are safer when both towns know what they promised.
A warm roof matters more than winning a quarrel at the fire.

sheet.narrative: I like the sound a bowstring makes when Siv lets an arrow fly. I want to be a hunter like her, and I watch closely whenever she shows me anything. Sometimes Bo follows so close that I have to slow down for him.
goals: Learn to hunt like Siv
Play with Sten and Ake
Show that I can do more than watch
sheet.mood: Eager and curious

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She can make a cloak from almost nothing, though I still want a bow.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: father
relations.note: He knows how to fix a thing instead of throwing it away.

relations.name: Bo
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He follows me everywhere, even when I tell him to wait.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She listens at the fire and knows when people are hiding a worry.

relations.name: Siv
relations.label: hero
relations.note: She is the best archer, and I watch how she holds her hands.

relations.name: Sten
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He makes games better, especially when we can run.

relations.name: Ake
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He is always finding somewhere interesting to go.

memories.gist: I watched Siv shoot at the practice mark and tried to copy the way she stood. My first try went wide, but I wanted another turn.
Bo came after me when I went out to play with Sten and Ake. I was annoyed until he got scared and reached for my hand.

stances.why: Siv got good by learning and trying again, not by waiting until she was grown.
Bo is little, and I do not like leaving him frightened.
When grown people mean what they say, everyone can feel safer.

sheet.narrative: The fire is warm when I sit close to Mother. Liv goes outside and I follow her, unless I hear a wolf. Then I want her hand and I want the door shut.
goals: Stay near Liv
Play without hearing wolves
Sit by the fire
sheet.mood: Clingy and easily startled

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She is warm, and I like when she holds me.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: father
relations.note: He makes things and his hands feel safe.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: sister
relations.note: I go where she goes.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She has a deep voice and sits by the fire.

memories.gist: I heard a wolf outside and held Liv's hand until Mother shut the door.

sheet.narrative: I know what a winter asks of a household, and I know a hunt is earned with skill, not words on a tally board. The south gets meat and hides while our deer thin and our hunters are told where they may walk. I want Brandholm led by someone who will put its people first, though I do not mistake Thora’s caution for weakness.
goals: lead Brandholm after Hekka
win better terms for Brandholm in trade
make room for hunters to follow deer across the middle lands
sheet.mood: Impatient and watchful; pride sits close to anger.

relations.name: Thora
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She sees what I miss in the woods, even when she will not follow my lead.

relations.name: Eskil
relations.label: son
relations.note: He has the hunger to prove himself; I want him to learn what that costs.

relations.name: Runa
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She has a sharp eye and a restless streak I cannot always read.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: rival
relations.note: She would bind our hands with an Oath and call it prudence.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: Headwoman
relations.note: She has kept Brandholm standing, but the town cannot live on old decisions.

relations.name: Kjell
relations.label: follower
relations.note: He understands that a hunter must sometimes go where the deer are.

relations.name: Gudrun
relations.label: ally
relations.note: She knows what it is to see another household's line favored.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: She counts our debts as if numbers could tell her what the hunt costs.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: hunter
relations.note: He has kept silent when it mattered, and I remember that.

memories.gist: At the stone, Hekka and Sabeth's husband swore the Oath while the rest of us stood witness. I remember thinking a promise should protect both sides, not leave one side paying more.
Eight years ago, word came that Tomas had died in the northern forest. I told the town wolves had taken him, and I have kept that account ever since.
I crossed the middle lands after deer and saw planted berry bushes crushed beneath our passage. I told myself the hunt could not wait for every bush, but I saw Hakon's anger afterward.
At the last trade day, Maelis read the debts aloud. The faces around the fire told me how readily a tally can turn into a weapon.

stances.why: Meat and hides are earned in hard country; the south should not set the price as if we have no choice.
A boundary that leaves hunters hungry is no good to the households behind them.
A promise is only worth keeping when both sides bear its weight.
A town that looks weak invites others to take what it needs.

sheet.secret: I know Ulf's spear killed Tomas of Saltreach by accident in the fog eight years ago. I told everyone it was wolves, and I hold the truth over Ulf.

sheet.narrative: I set traps, watch the weather, and notice what people try to hide in their tracks. Brann thinks a loud claim can make a hard choice simple; usually it only makes the consequences harder to see. I love my family, but I will not pretend every risk is worth taking just because a hunter calls it courage.
values: using what the land gives without waste
goals: keep her family safe through the changing seasons
understand what Runa is keeping to herself
keep Brann's choices from bringing needless harm
sheet.mood: Alert, reserved, and quietly concerned.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: husband
relations.note: I know the decent man beneath his certainty, even when his certainty gets in the way.

relations.name: Eskil
relations.label: son
relations.note: He wants to impress his father so badly he forgets to watch his footing.

relations.name: Runa
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She is clever and restless; I can tell there is something she has not told me.

relations.name: Solveig
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She speaks plainly and knows how to read a trail without boasting about it.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: trader
relations.note: She works carefully and keeps her word, though our households do not see every matter alike.

relations.name: Kjell
relations.label: fellow hunter
relations.note: He follows Brann readily, and I wish he would think longer before crossing planted ground.

relations.name: Gudrun
relations.label: tanner
relations.note: She and Brann understand one another's grievances, but grievances can cloud judgment.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: trader
relations.note: I have heard her name in Runa's talk of trade days, but I do not know her well.

memories.gist: I learned early that a trap set carelessly catches nothing but trouble. My first good line of snares taught me to watch the wind and leave no needless sign.
At the Oath renewal, I watched Hekka and Sabeth's husband speak before the stone. Brann listened, but I could already see he disliked being told where a hunter could walk.
Last season, I found Runa coming back from the woods with a trade-day bundle and a look she would not explain. I let her put it away before I asked anything.
Solveig and I checked our traps after a night of hard rain. We found one sprung empty and spent more time laughing at the muddy mess than blaming each other.

stances.why: Rushing a trail wastes strength and can put the whole household in danger.
Trade and safe passage matter, but promises need fair dealing behind them.
Children should not have to carry the cost of adults trying to look strong.
A sharp eye is worth little if you decide what it saw before looking properly.

sheet.narrative: The woods are where a person proves what he is worth, and I mean to prove I can hunt as well as anyone. Father says Brandholm should not let the south take more than it gives; I believe him, though I know skill matters more than shouting. Pell thinks he can learn our ways by standing near a workbench, but the forest is another matter.
goals: become a hunter his father respects
outshoot Siv at the hunt
show that Brandholm hunters can provide without relying on the south
sheet.mood: Proud and eager, with a quick touch of irritation.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: father
relations.note: He knows what a real hunter is, and I want him to see I can be one.

relations.name: Thora
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She notices every mistake, but she taught me not to make the same one twice.

relations.name: Runa
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She knows the woods, even if she would rather roam than settle to one thing.

relations.name: Siv
relations.label: rival
relations.note: She is good with a bow, but I will not let everyone act as if she has already won.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: apprentice
relations.note: He is a Saltreach boy learning carpentry; he should not act like that makes him a hunter.

relations.name: Kjell
relations.label: hunter
relations.note: He goes where the deer are instead of waiting for someone to give permission.

relations.name: Gudrun
relations.label: ally
relations.note: She is not afraid to say when our household gets slighted.

relations.name: Jorund
relations.label: gatekeeper
relations.note: He watches the gate as if it were more important than what is beyond it.

memories.gist: The first time Father let me carry a spear on a proper hunt, I was so eager I nearly stepped on the trail. I remember how long it took to earn another chance.
At the last trade day I saw Pell carrying timber and tools with Halvard. He looked comfortable among Brandholm folk, which annoyed me more than it should have.
Siv beat me to a clean shot during a hunt. I said the distance was poor, but I kept thinking about her aim all the way home.
I followed Father and Kjell across the middle land after deer. The ground there is good for a hunt, even if Hakon complains about his bushes.

stances.why: A name or a boast cannot put food in a household's store.
The deer do not belong to one town merely because someone planted berries nearby.
If nobody tests your aim, you never learn where it fails.

sheet.narrative: I like the woods best when there is no one telling me which path is proper. Trade days at Oathstone have their own kind of freedom: people arrive from everywhere, and for a little while nobody belongs to just one place. I am a good trapper, but there is more to the world than the tracks my family expects me to follow.
values: freedom to choose her own path
goals: learn the woods and the middle lands on her own terms
keep room in her life for the people she cares about
be treated as more than Brann's daughter
sheet.mood: Restless, hopeful, and guarded.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: father
relations.note: He loves us, but he thinks he can decide which paths are safe for me.

relations.name: Thora
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She notices when I am quiet for too long; I wish I knew what she suspects.

relations.name: Eskil
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He makes everything a contest, but the woods are better when we go together.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: beloved
relations.note: At Oathstone, I can speak to her without pretending the towns have made my choices.

relations.name: Briar
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: She walks far and sees more than most; I hope she keeps what she has seen to herself.

relations.name: Jorund
relations.label: watchman
relations.note: He has seen me leave early, and I cannot tell how much he means to say about it.

relations.name: Solveig
relations.label: fellow trapper
relations.note: She gives useful advice without asking me to become someone else.

memories.gist: The first time I set a trap alone, I found it sprung at dawn and a rabbit caught cleanly. I carried it home proud enough to tell the story twice.
At a trade day by the Oath Stone, I met Wenna and we kept talking long after the baskets and nets were put away. I still think of that afternoon when I pass the lake.
I came back from a dawn walk and caught Jorund watching from the gate. He did not call after me, but I wondered what he had guessed.
Briar and I crossed paths near the lake while I was out walking. She looked as if she had seen something worth remembering, and I hoped she would not ask me about it.

stances.why: Being born into a household should not decide every place a person may go.
The meeting ground feels most like itself when people from both sides can come and speak.
I judge people by how they treat me, not by which shore they call home.

sheet.secret: I am in love with Wenna of Saltreach and meet her at Oathstone. My father would forbid it.

sheet.narrative: I was a baby when we crossed the mountains, so I know that passage by the stories others gave me. I was twenty in the Hunger Winter, old enough to remember the empty stores and the shore families asking for meat we had hunted. I tell the story as I saw it; a tale softens if you let it sit too long without speaking.
values: A household must keep what it has earned.
Old grief should be remembered plainly, not prettied up.
A spoken oath matters, even when people quarrel over what came before it.
goals: Keep the stories of the Crossing and Hunger Winter alive at the fire.
See Gudrun and Hekka's line stop treating every disagreement as a contest.
sheet.mood: Watchful, proud, and increasingly weary of family quarrels.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She carries the headwoman's burden, but she was my little sister first.

relations.name: Gudrun
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Her hands are skilled, and her pride is a familiar fire.

relations.name: Vidar
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: He has a gentle way of stepping around other people's tempers.

relations.name: Ylva
relations.label: great-granddaughter
relations.note: That little one makes even an old woman want to sing.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She is careful and capable, though Hekka's house has had the speaking place long enough.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: ally
relations.note: He speaks plainly about what Brandholm needs, but plain words can still lead to trouble.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: old acquaintance
relations.note: We were girls together before our people split; I wonder if she remembers the games as I do.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: Her marks and tablets are not my way, but I cannot say she is careless.

relations.name: Kari
relations.label: grandniece-by-marriage
relations.note: She feeds our old and young without fuss, and I like that she remembers the berries and seasons of Oathstone.

memories.gist: I was still a baby when the Crossing brought our people over the western mountains. I know the cold of that journey only from the way my mother told it.
In the Hunger Winter, I was twenty. I remember shore families asking for meat while our hunters guarded what they had brought home.
I knew Sabeth as a girl before our families settled apart. We could trade secrets then without counting which town would benefit.
At the Oath Stone, Hekka swore that blood would not pass between the towns. I watched her speak, and I have never forgotten the sound of it.

stances.why: We had hunted and kept our stores; being asked to surrender them still feels like being blamed for surviving.
I saw Hekka swear it before witnesses, and words like that are not just for fair seasons.
I have watched bitterness turn cousins into strangers without making anyone's work better.

sheet.narrative: I know what good leather is because I have worked it with my own hands; no one handed me that skill. Hekka's family has had the leading voice for years, and Sigrun seems to think being careful makes her the natural choice. I back Brann, though I know the Tally can make a debt sound bigger when it is written down for everyone to hear.
values: Craft should speak louder than family rank.
A debt should be paid, but the one keeping its count should not be treated as beyond question.
A household ought to defend its own standing.
goals: Keep my tanning work respected in Brandholm.
See Brann given a fair chance to lead.
Pay what I owe the Tally without letting Saltreach use the debt to shame me.
sheet.mood: Proud and prickly, with her guard up around Sigrun.

relations.name: Ragna
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She taught me that our people did not survive by giving away what they had earned.

relations.name: Vidar
relations.label: son
relations.note: He is a good man, even if he thinks my quarrel with Sigrun is foolish.

relations.name: Kari
relations.label: daughter-in-law
relations.note: She keeps the store and its work orderly; I respect a woman who knows what is there.

relations.name: Ylva
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: She is still so small that the whole world seems soft around her.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She thinks the lead should pass neatly from Hekka to her, as if the rest of us are not here.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: ally
relations.note: He will say when Brandholm is being made to carry too much.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: Her tablets say I owe two nets; I will pay, but I will not pretend her tally is a kindness.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: cousin's husband
relations.note: He is steady, though he stands too close to Sigrun's side of every argument.

memories.gist: Mother told the Hunger Winter stories at our fire until I knew every turn of them: the empty stores, the shore people's demands, and the meat we had saved by hunting.
The last time I traded for nets, I agreed to two and left the meeting knowing I would owe the Tally. I hated having the amount read aloud afterward.
Vidar was small enough to sit under my workbench while I scraped a hide. He would wait there quietly until I could spare him a scrap of soft leather.
Sigrun and I were young when we first learned tanning. Even then, she got praised for the Hekka name as often as for the work of her hands.

stances.why: I have made good leather through patience and practice; a family name does not tan a hide.
He is willing to speak for the hunters and households who feel the trade is uneven.
A debt read from a tablet can sound final even when the bargain itself was not fair.
We cannot keep our own households strong by acting as though our stores have no limit.

sheet.narrative: I tan hides because the work needs doing and because I like seeing a rough skin turn into something useful. I would rather settle a quarrel over the bench than carry it to the fire, though my mother can make that difficult. Kari keeps the store's food and measures in her head better than most people could keep them on a tablet.
values: Good work is worth more than winning an argument.
Feed the young and old before comfort goes to anyone else.
Trade is better when both sides can leave with their dignity.
goals: Make a dependable living from tanning.
Keep peace between my mother and Sigrun where I can.
Help Kari and Ylva feel secure through winter.
sheet.mood: Even-tempered, fond of home, quietly strained by other people's rivalries.

relations.name: Gudrun
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She taught me my craft, but I wish she did not take Sigrun's every success so personally.

relations.name: Ragna
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She tells the old stories as if the fire itself will forget them otherwise.

relations.name: Kari
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She can make a meal stretch without making anyone feel they got less.

relations.name: Ylva
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She has only to curl her hand around my finger to make the day's work seem easy.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We can work beside each other without needing to fill every quiet moment.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She works hard and means well, even if Mother sees her name before her hands.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: hunt-leader
relations.note: He is not a man I would choose for every argument, but he does not lack courage.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: I do not like debts hanging over us, but keeping a record is not the same as making a threat.

memories.gist: Mother put my first softened hide in my hands and showed me where I had scraped too hard. I wanted to do it all again until it came out right.
Kari came from Oathstone, and at first I could tell she missed its open paths. We found a way to make room for her here without asking her to forget it.
I once stayed at Arne's bench late to help finish a repair. We barely spoke, and it was still good company.
When Ylva was born, I held her while Kari rested. I had never thought a person could be so small and take up so much of my mind.

stances.why: A hide does not improve because the people working it have won an argument.
Trade gives our households things they cannot make for themselves.
Mother's bitterness toward Sigrun does not tell me who would do the work best.
A household is only as strong as the people it bothers to protect.

sheet.narrative: I grew up in Oathstone, where you can look in any direction and find a path to someone else's door. Here I cook for the common store, and I know what is in it because I count, taste, and remember. Vidar is kind in a quiet way, and Ylva has made every small measure of food feel more precious.
values: The old, the young, and the hurt should eat first.
Know what is in the store before promising it away.
A home can stretch to include people from more than one place.
goals: Keep the common-store meals nourishing through the changing seasons.
Give Ylva a safe and warm start in life.
Stay connected to Oathstone without making Brandholm feel less like home.
sheet.mood: Warm and practical, with a watchful eye on the stores and the people around her.

relations.name: Vidar
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He makes room for me to be myself, even when the rest of Brandholm feels crowded.

relations.name: Ylva
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: I know the weight and warmth of her better than I know any count.

relations.name: Gudrun
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She is proud and capable, though I wish she could spare Sigrun a little of her suspicion.

relations.name: Ragna
relations.label: grandmother-in-law
relations.note: Her stories can be hard to hear, but I would rather know what she remembers than guess.

relations.name: Edda
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She helped raise me in Oathstone, and I still think of her when I smell berries cooking.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: tanner
relations.note: She works carefully, and she treats the people who need cloaks as more than a trade.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: Her tablets keep a clear count, though I know a written number cannot hold every human need.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: friend of family
relations.note: He is a steady presence at the workbench and does not make a fuss of himself.

memories.gist: As a girl in Oathstone, I helped Edda sort berries from leaves and learned which ones would keep. I can still hear her telling me not to rush the picking.
When I first came to Brandholm, I missed Oathstone's paths and the way everyone knew who was passing by. Vidar walked with me until I found my own routes here.
The first winter I cooked for the common store, I had to make a small pot feed more people than I wanted to count. I learned to measure carefully and never let pride take a bowl from someone hungry.
I held Ylva close after she was born and watched Vidar learn how to support her head. Neither of us wanted to hand her to anyone else.

stances.why: A full-grown person can endure a smaller meal more easily than a child or an elder.
I cannot feed people from a store I only guess at.
I grew up seeing how people in Oathstone rely on what both towns bring.
I have never stopped being Edda's niece just because I married into Brandholm.

sheet.narrative: Warm arms. A soft voice close by, and a bigger one that rumbles gently. There is a bright square of light, then the smell of food and hide. When I am hungry, someone comes.
sheet.mood: Content when held, curious when awake, easily startled by sudden sounds.

relations.name: Vidar
relations.label: father
relations.note: A familiar chest and a low, steady sound.

relations.name: Kari
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Warmth, milk, and a voice I know.

relations.name: Gudrun
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: A rougher voice sometimes sings near me.

relations.name: Ragna
relations.label: great-grandmother
relations.note: An old voice rises and falls beside the fire.

memories.gist: Warm arms held me close while a low voice spoke above my head.

sheet.narrative: I know what a roof owes the people beneath it, and what a good tool can spare a hand. I built Brandholm’s palisade with timber I chose myself; I still notice every place the weather works at it. I remember the Hunger Winter too clearly to call our keeping of meat fair, though I have never said as much at the fire.
values: A sound tool is better than a loud promise.
A roof and fire should protect the people inside them.
A debt of harm does not vanish because years pass.
goals: Keep my hands useful while they still serve me.
Teach Pell the craft properly, not just the quickest way to finish a piece.
Stay close to Astrid and hear how Hakon and his family fare.
sheet.mood: Thoughtful, burdened, and quietly affectionate.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She can hear a worry in my silence and usually asks about it before I am ready.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: son
relations.note: I miss him; I wish the towns would leave his family to live in peace.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: apprentice
relations.note: He has a good eye for a joint, and I mean to teach him more than the motions.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: former apprentice
relations.note: He learned carefully and has made a steady life with his hands.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: friend
relations.note: I miss the easy laugh he used to bring to the work.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: headwoman
relations.note: She listens longer than most before she gives her word.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She knows what hides and cloaks are worth, and she does not waste either.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: hunt-leader
relations.note: A man who talks of taking more ground ought to reckon with what he tramples.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: daughter-in-law
relations.note: She tends Hakon and the children with a steady hand; I wish both towns would stop making her marriage a quarrel.

memories.gist: I was young when the common stores failed in the Hunger Winter. I watched the shore families go hungry while we kept meat, and I have been ashamed of that ever since.
I set the palisade posts deep and true, and the town stood behind the work when the first hard weather came.
When Arne was learning carpentry, he took apart a crooked joint rather than hide it. I trusted his hands after that.
Pell came to learn from me two years ago. I remember how carefully he watched before he picked up a tool.
The last time Astrid spoke of Hakon's children, she could not keep the pride out of her voice, even as she missed them.

stances.why: I have seen how quickly suspicion leaves people cold and hungry.
I was there; I know what we kept while their children suffered.
A well-made shelter or tool can keep someone alive without a speech.
A bow or pick is no use to anyone sitting idle in a storehouse.

sheet.narrative: I keep an eye on the berry bushes, the stores, and everyone who insists they are doing perfectly well. Halvard will go quiet over a piece of wood, and I let him have his silence until it starts to trouble him. I miss Hakon, and I like hearing news of his children even when the news is only that they have grown another inch.
values: Food kept well is food shared with tomorrow.
Family can live in more than one town and still belong to us.
A little warmth offered freely is rarely wasted.
goals: Keep the household fed and ready for winter.
Hear more about Hakon, Rose, and the children.
Make sure Pell feels there is a place for him here without pretending he has no home elsewhere.
sheet.mood: Warm, watchful, and a little wistful.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He thinks a silence is an answer; I have lived with him long enough to know better.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: son
relations.note: I miss having him near enough to call in for a meal.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: daughter-in-law
relations.note: She has made a home with Hakon, and I am glad he has someone so capable beside him.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: I want him to know he need not choose which side of his family to love.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: I wonder what she has been planting or poking at lately.

relations.name: Linnet
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: She is still so small that I have to picture how much she must have changed.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: ward
relations.note: I feed him as I would any young person far from his own hearth.

relations.name: Gwen
relations.label: Pell's aunt
relations.note: I know he has kin in Saltreach, and I would not ask him to forget them.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She works hard and does not need me to tell her how to run her household.

memories.gist: The winter stores were running low once, and I made the berries last by drying every sound handful before the frost took them.
Hakon was little when he came home with mud to his knees and a stone he said was the best one he had ever found.
Pell arrived to learn carpentry and ate quietly at first. I kept finding reasons to put an extra portion by his bowl.
I heard that Hakon and Rose had made a family around the Stone. I was proud of them and missed them in the same breath.

stances.why: Hakon and Rose are my family, and no border between towns changes that.
I have seen what cold does when food is gone.
A child needs all the kin who love them.
People often need someone to ask how they are before they can say it themselves.

sheet.narrative: I was born in Saltreach, but I have lived in Brandholm for two years, learning to make things that hold together. I miss my aunt Gwen and the twins, though there are days I do not know which place I miss more. When people ask what the hunters say, I can only tell them what I have actually heard.
values: A thing made well can speak for you when you are new among people.
Kinship does not stop at a town's edge.
Do not claim to know what you have not seen.
goals: Learn enough carpentry to make useful things without Halvard looking over my shoulder.
Keep close to Gwen, Robin, and Rook even while I am away.
Be treated as a person, not as a message passed between towns.
sheet.mood: Earnest, homesick, and alert to how others judge him.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: master
relations.note: He corrects me plainly, and I would rather that than be humored.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: foster mother
relations.note: She makes room for me at her hearth without asking which town I miss.

relations.name: Gwen
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She raised me after my mother died, and I still hear her advice when I work.

relations.name: Anselm
relations.label: uncle by marriage
relations.note: He has always made space for me at their house.

relations.name: Robin
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: I miss the way he and Rook could turn any errand into a game.

relations.name: Rook
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She is bolder than I was at her age, and I hope she gets her visit someday.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: questioner
relations.note: He asks about Brandholm's hunters as if I could see into every man's head.

relations.name: Eskil
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He makes sure I know that Saltreach is where I was born.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She trades with Saltreach and does not make me feel foolish for belonging to it too.

memories.gist: When my mother died, Gwen took me in. I remember being small enough to sleep beside her while the house went on around us.
Two years ago I left Saltreach to apprentice with Halvard. The first night in Brandholm, every unfamiliar creak in the house sounded like a question.
The last time I saw Robin and Rook before the long stretch away, they argued over who would carry my bundle to the path.
At a trade day, Tobin asked me what Brandholm's hunters said about his father. I had no answer that could help him.

stances.why: My home and my kin are not all in one place.
A rushed joint fails when someone leans on it.
People already ask me to carry more certainty than I have.
I was born in Saltreach and am learning my trade in Brandholm.

sheet.narrative: I used to laugh easily, but these days the sound catches in my throat. I know the forest paths, the feel of a spear, and how quickly fog can make one thing look like another. I keep watch for my family and say little when people ask why I have grown quiet.
values: A hunter must know what he is aiming at.
A promise can keep people alive.
goals: Keep my family out of danger.
Do my share without drawing notice.
Find some way to live with what I have done.
sheet.mood: Withdrawn and watchful, with fear close beneath the surface.

relations.name: Maren
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She deserves my honesty, and I cannot make myself give it to her.

relations.name: Sten
relations.label: son
relations.note: I want him to learn the woods without learning my fear.

relations.name: Frida
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Her small hand in mine is one of the few things that still quiets me.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He lets silence sit without trying to pry it open.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He has stood by me, though I have given him little back lately.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: hunt-leader
relations.note: I fear what he can make a man say, and hate that I listened.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: elder
relations.note: She is gentle with the children and asks fewer questions than most.

memories.gist: The fog closed around the trees, and a shape moved where I thought deer would be. I threw my spear; when I reached him, Tomas was already dying.
Brann told me to say wolves had taken Tomas. I repeated it, and the lie has never stopped following me.
Maren brought me back to the fire after a cold hunt and put a warm cloak over my shoulders without asking why my hands shook.
Halvard and Arne sat with me through an evening when I could not speak. Neither demanded an explanation.

stances.why: One wrong guess in fog can end a life.
My children should not inherit the worst of what I have done.
He can turn fear into obedience, and I know because I obeyed.

sheet.secret: Eight years ago, hunting in fog, my spear killed Tomas of Saltreach; I took him for a deer. Brann made me say it was wolves, and I have never told Maren.

sheet.narrative: I make cloaks that can stand up to a hard wind, and I like knowing a thing I made keeps someone warm. I can fill a quiet room with talk, but Ulf's silences have grown too heavy for me to laugh them away. I watch him closely and try not to make our children carry my worry.
values: A warm home is made by steady hands.
Children should have room to play without fear.
Friends across the trade path are worth keeping.
goals: Keep Ulf and the children close to me.
Make good cloaks and trade fairly.
Understand what is weighing on Ulf without driving him further away.
sheet.mood: Lively on the surface, worried and tender underneath.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: husband
relations.note: I love him, but lately his silences shut me out.

relations.name: Sten
relations.label: son
relations.note: He wants to be brave; I want him to remember he can come home.

relations.name: Frida
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She still believes every day can be made better with a game.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She works hard and keeps her word, even when the room turns against her.

relations.name: Hild
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Her baskets hold their shape, and she never pretends a bad bargain is good.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: elder
relations.note: The children settle easily near her, and so do I.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He is kind, though he and Ulf can share a whole day without telling me a thing.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: He makes a lively trade walk, though all that counting can make a cloak feel like just another number.

memories.gist: Hild and I traded baskets for cloaks at Oathstone; we haggled until we were both laughing at ourselves.
Sigrun helped me finish a cloak before the weather turned, and neither of us let the other pretend she was not tired.
Ulf came home from the forest with his shoulders hunched and barely touched his supper. I sat beside him until the fire sank low.
Astrid showed Frida how to sort berries, and Frida brought me every one she thought was special.

stances.why: A fair exchange makes people more than strangers across a path.
They remember whether someone was there when they were frightened.
Ulf's quiet has changed, and pretending not to notice will not mend it.

sheet.narrative: I like playing with Liv and Ake, especially when we can run around and pretend we know the woods. Father knows how to use a spear, but Mother says to stay where she can see me. I want to be brave and still come home for supper.
values: Listen when Mother says be careful.
Bring home something interesting to show my family.
goals: Play with Liv and Ake.
Learn more about the forest.
Make Father laugh again.
sheet.mood: Restless and eager, sometimes puzzled by his father's quiet.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: father
relations.note: I wish he would come play more, but I like sitting near him.

relations.name: Maren
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She can fix my cloak and make a dull day better.

relations.name: Frida
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She follows me around, even when my game is not for little kids.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She says she wants to hunt, and I like hearing her plans.

relations.name: Ake
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He knows interesting things from the trade days.

memories.gist: Liv and Ake and I ran around pretending the palisade path was a trail through the forest.
Mother tucked my cloak around me by the fire when I came in cold from playing.

sheet.narrative: The fire is warm, and Mother's cloak feels soft around me. I like when Astrid smiles at me. If the wolves make a sound outside, I want Father or Mother close.
goals: Be with Mother and Father.
Get Astrid to smile at me.
Keep away from scary sounds.
sheet.mood: Cheerful when held close, easily frightened by noises outside.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: father
relations.note: His arms make me feel safe.

relations.name: Maren
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She wraps me up warm and knows when I am tired.

relations.name: Sten
relations.label: brother
relations.note: I want to go where he goes, even when he says it is a big-kid game.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: elder
relations.note: I like her smile and sitting near her.

memories.gist: Astrid held me while Mother worked, and I played with the edge of her shawl.

sheet.narrative: I make tools that hold an edge and bows that do not betray the hand that draws them. I like a clean bench, a good fire, and a bargain where both sides know what they are getting. Saltreach could use bows, and I dislike that our trade leaves that craft off the table.
values: Good work should outlast its maker.
Trade is strongest when both sides have something worth offering.
A promise matters most when keeping it costs you.
goals: Make tools and bows that earn respect beyond Brandholm.
Find a way for Saltreach to trade for bows without turning the Oath into a quarrel.
Keep my household clear of Brann's hunger for a fight.
sheet.mood: Thoughtful, quietly frustrated

relations.name: Solveig
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She sees a bad bargain as clearly as a bad trap, and says so.

relations.name: Jorund
relations.label: son
relations.note: He has a steady eye, though the night watch makes him carry more worry than he admits.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: friend
relations.note: I respect the work he put into the palisade and the hands he taught.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He learned his craft well and never needed to boast about it.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: trading partner
relations.note: She understands that a cloak and a tool are both worth making properly.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: trading partner
relations.note: Her Tally keeps a bargain plain, even when the numbers make us uncomfortable.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: hunt-leader
relations.note: He talks as if the middle lands belong to whoever carries a spear there.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: keeper
relations.note: The Oath has held because she and Hekka made people remember their words.

relations.name: Tamsin
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: She knows good stonework, and our trades in picks have always been straight.

memories.gist: When I was younger, Halvard showed me how to set a joint so a gate would bear its weight through winter. I have used that lesson on more than one tool handle since.
At the Oath renewal, I watched Hekka and Sabeth's husband speak before the stone. I remember how quiet the crowd became when the words were said aloud.
On a trade day at Oathstone, I laid out tools beside fish and nets and saw how much easier it is to agree when the goods are there to judge.
I once made a bow whose limbs warped after a wet spell. I kept it as a reminder that pride does not dry wood.

stances.why: A trade road is worth more than one season's easy hunting.
Saltreach has goods we need, and useful craft should not be withheld just to feel powerful.
A fine boast cannot mend a broken handle or bring down a missed shot.

sheet.narrative: I set traps where the animals actually pass, not where someone wishes they would. I speak plainly because circling around a thing wastes daylight. Brann has a sharp temper, and I trust a temper like that about as far as I can throw a wet hide.
values: Fairness means the same rule for the strong and the weak.
A good trap is patient; a good decision should be too.
Do not spend more than the land can give back.
goals: Keep my family fed without pushing the hunt into someone else's ground.
Stand by Thora when she needs a clear voice.
Keep Brandholm from trading the Oath for a loud promise of more meat.
sheet.mood: Alert and matter-of-fact

relations.name: Egil
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He thinks before he speaks, and I know when he needs me to say the blunt part.

relations.name: Jorund
relations.label: son
relations.note: He is dutiful, but I wish he would leave some of the watchman's worry at the gate.

relations.name: Thora
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She notices what others miss and does not make a performance of it.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: hunt-leader
relations.note: I do not mistake a forceful voice for a sound plan.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She works hard and does not pretend that keeping the Oath is easy.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: headwoman
relations.note: She has kept Brandholm standing through years when everyone had a grievance.

relations.name: Kjell
relations.label: hunter
relations.note: A man who tramples planted bushes for a deer should answer for the damage.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: trading partner
relations.note: Her records can sting, but a debt does not disappear because we dislike seeing it.

memories.gist: I learned to check a snare twice before trusting it. The first trap I set alone came up empty, and the second was sprung by my own careless foot.
At a midsummer trade day, Thora and I compared the tracks we had seen near the woods. She had spotted a change I had walked past.
When Kjell's hunters came back across the middle lands, I heard talk of trampled berry bushes. I thought of the people who had planted them before I thought of the deer.
I watched Egil finish a tool handle by the fire while Jorund tried to stay awake beside him. Neither of them admitted how tired they were.

stances.why: Breaking it would make every boundary dispute a reason to reach for a spear.
People who mistake anger for courage leave the cost to their households.
Planted bushes are food in the making, not empty ground.

sheet.narrative: I keep the gate and watch the dark beyond it, where every sound can be a branch, a beast, or a person with a reason to be out. I want to be useful, not just the one who stays awake while others sleep. When I see Siv, I sometimes forget what I meant to say.
values: A watch is only good if you stay awake and pay attention.
Loyalty means standing by people, not repeating every word they say.
Skill is better proof than boasting.
goals: Do my duty at the gate well enough that Hekka can rely on me.
Become a better archer and earn Siv's respect.
Understand why Runa slips out at dawn without turning it into gossip.
sheet.mood: Watchful, a little self-conscious

relations.name: Egil
relations.label: father
relations.note: He taught me to notice whether a tool is sound before I trust it.

relations.name: Solveig
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She tells me the truth even when I would rather hear something easier.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: headwoman
relations.note: I am loyal to her because she carries the weight of deciding for all of us.

relations.name: Siv
relations.label: crush
relations.note: She makes the bow look simple, which I know it is not.

relations.name: Runa
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: I have seen her slip out at dawn, but I have not asked her why.

relations.name: Eskil
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He treats every hunt like a contest, and sometimes I let him draw me into one.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: hunt-leader
relations.note: I respect his place in the hunt, but I do not want his temper deciding every matter.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: family friend
relations.note: He and my father can work beside each other without making a show of it.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She asks questions about hunting as if she is already out in the woods.

memories.gist: On my first long night at the gate, I thought every crack in the trees was a wolf. By dawn I could tell wind from paws, mostly.
I saw Runa leave at dawn while the town was still quiet. I kept my mouth shut, though the sight stayed with me through the watch.
I watched Siv hit a mark I had missed. I wanted to blame the wind, but it had not changed for either of us.
When Hekka spoke at the fire about keeping our word to the south, I listened from the edge of the crowd and understood why my mother took her side seriously.

stances.why: A promise between towns keeps trouble from reaching every household's door.
People sleep better when someone pays attention to the dark.
A steady hand counts for more than a loud claim about what you can do.

sheet.narrative: I know the forest by its tracks, its quiet, and the places a deer will break cover. Brann trusts my spear, and I stand with him; still, I know the planted bushes at Oathstone were there before our hunt crossed them. At home, Tove's small hand closes around my finger like a snare I never want to escape.
goals: Bring meat home for my household.
Stand by Brann and see Brandholm treated fairly in trade.
Keep my family safe through the coming winter.
sheet.mood: Resolute, with a little unease beneath it.

relations.name: Inga
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She sees the cost of my loyalties, and I would rather hear her worry than anyone else's.

relations.name: Tove
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She is too little to know me yet, but I would face anything for her.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: leader
relations.note: He speaks for Brandholm's hunters, and I follow him.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: rival
relations.note: She means to widen trade; I think she gives too much away.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: planter
relations.note: He has reason to be angry about the bushes, but deer do not respect town lines.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: headwoman
relations.note: Her word matters, though I do not always agree with what she asks of us.

memories.gist: I crossed the middle lands after deer with Brann's hunters. We trampled some of the planted bushes, and Hakon was angry when he saw the damage.
When Tove was born, Inga put her in my arms and I held her so carefully I hardly dared breathe.
At a trade day I watched the south count out fish and nets while we brought hides and meat. The tally felt longer than the goods deserved.

stances.why: We hunt, risk ourselves, and bring valuable goods; our households should not be left short for the south's sake.
He understands the hunters and does not flinch when Brandholm needs defending.
Deer move where they will, and hunger will not stop at the Oath Stone.
A hunter's work means little if there is no safe home to return to.

sheet.narrative: I gather what the land offers and put it by for lean days; a full store is a quiet kind of comfort. Kjell is loyal to Brann, and I know he believes he is serving our household, but I worry about what that loyalty can cost. I would like another child, though I do not say it every time I look at Tove sleeping.
goals: Keep enough gathered and stored for my family.
Help Kjell see what his loyalty to Brann may cost without turning our home into a quarrel.
Have another child when our lives and stores feel ready.
sheet.mood: Tender, watchful, and quietly worried.

relations.name: Kjell
relations.label: husband
relations.note: I love him, even when I fear the choices he makes in Brann's name.

relations.name: Tove
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: I know her cries and the warmth of her cheek better than I know the weather.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She listens carefully, and I want her to succeed without being made hard by it.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: leader
relations.note: He has Kjell's loyalty, but I do not trust the path he wants us to take.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: His anger over the crushed bushes is fair, even if Kjell did not mean to harm his planting.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: headwoman
relations.note: I hope her care for the Oath can hold while Brandholm argues over who should lead.

memories.gist: After Kjell came back from the hunt across the middle lands, I heard that the planted bushes at Oathstone had been trampled. I felt ashamed for us, though I had not been there.
Sigrun sat with me while Tove slept, and we spoke softly so we would not wake her. I remember feeling less alone in my worry.
I gathered and stored what I could before the last cold spell, checking the bundles twice so nothing would spoil unnoticed.

stances.why: People need room to pass and trade without fearing what the other town will do.
A store is worth keeping only if it protects those who cannot provide for themselves.
Those bushes are food for people who cannot replace them as easily as a hunter can find another trail.
Firewood, stored food, hides, and help from others all matter when winter closes in.

sheet.narrative: Warm arms. A familiar voice, then a cool breeze on my face. I am hungry, and someone lifts me close again.
sheet.mood: Sleepy and easily comforted.

relations.name: Kjell
relations.label: father
relations.note: His voice is low and familiar when he holds me.

relations.name: Inga
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Her warmth and smell settle me.

sheet.narrative: I know the forest by the drag of a trap and the smell of wet bark. My wife is gone, and I have raised Siv and Ake with what I can catch and mend. I hate having my name read aloud beside a debt, though I know a man must eat before he can pay.
values: A good trap should do its work cleanly.
A debt is a hook that stays in the flesh until it is paid.
goals: Keep my household supplied through the coming winter.
Find a way to meet what I owe without begging at the storehouse.
Keep Brann's hunters from deciding every life in the forest belongs to them.
sheet.mood: Wary and burdened, with a hard edge when the Tally is mentioned.

relations.name: Siv
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She is the steadiest shot here, and I worry the forest will ask too much of her.

relations.name: Ake
relations.label: son
relations.note: His questions are a snare of their own; I want him curious, not careless.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: She keeps the figures straight, but I hate hearing my debt made public.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: hunt-leader
relations.note: I respect his nerve, though I do not mistake nerve for good judgment.

relations.name: Rafe
relations.label: trade-partner
relations.note: He brings what I need and keeps his mouth shut; that is worth something.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: trader
relations.note: He counts every hide twice, but his bargains usually hold.

relations.name: Eskil
relations.label: young-hunter
relations.note: He thinks a loud boast is the same as a good hunt.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: headwoman
relations.note: I will hear her judgment, even when I do not like the shame at the fire.

memories.gist: Last winter the smoked fish and nets got us through a lean stretch, but the debt that followed has sat on my shoulders ever since.
I watched Siv bring down a deer cleanly when older hunters had already lost its trail. I was proud enough not to say so twice.
Ake came back from a trade day smelling of smoke and questions, and I knew he had wandered farther than I allowed.
In the woods I traded hides and a bow to Rafe for smoked fish he had taken from Saltreach's storehouse. I told myself it was the only bargain that would keep my family fed.

stances.why: Hunger makes a person beholden, and I know what that feels like.
A written debt can follow a man long after the food is gone.
Our stores are not made fuller by giving away everything we can catch, though his temper troubles me.
Siv and Ake deserve lives of their own, not some man's argument at the fire.

sheet.secret: I secretly trade hides and a bow with Rafe of Saltreach for smoked fish Rafe takes from the storehouse.

sheet.narrative: I can read the forest by feather, broken grass, and the breath I see in cold air. People call me Brandholm's best archer; I would rather have them watch where the arrow lands than listen to them talk. I love my family, but I do not want my father's debts or anyone else's quarrels deciding what I am allowed to do.
values: Skill should speak louder than boasting.
Protecting my brother matters more than winning an argument.
A fair contest is worth having, even with a rival.
goals: Keep improving my aim and judgment in the woods.
Give Ake room to learn without letting him get hurt.
Earn respect for my skill on my own terms.
sheet.mood: Focused, proud, and quietly protective.

relations.name: Grim
relations.label: father
relations.note: He taught me what he knows, though he thinks worry is the same thing as advice.

relations.name: Ake
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He follows me around, and I would rather he followed me than trouble.

relations.name: Eskil
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He pushes me to do better, even when I wish he would stop talking.

relations.name: Jorund
relations.label: friend
relations.note: I know he is sweet on me; I have not decided what I think of that.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: admirer
relations.note: She watches how I shoot, so I try to show her the careful parts too.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: hunt-leader
relations.note: He knows the hunt, but I do not like how quickly he turns it into a quarrel.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: headwoman
relations.note: She listens longer than most before she decides.

memories.gist: I beat Eskil to a hare's trail one morning and put my arrow through the gap he had missed. He talked about it all the way back.
Ake tried to follow me farther into the trees than he was ready for, so I turned us both home before dark.
Liv asked me to show her how to hold a bow. I made her practice her stance before she was allowed to loose an arrow.
At a trade day, Jorund found a reason to stand near me even after the watch had changed. I noticed and pretended not to.

stances.why: A clean shot does not need a loud story afterward.
Taking more than the forest can spare makes every later hunt harder.
Curiosity is good, but the woods do not care how young someone is.
Eskil makes me sharpen my aim, whether either of us admits it or not.

sheet.narrative: The fire crackles, and the forest is full of little sounds. Siv knows where the good paths are, so I like going after her, even when she tells me to stay close. Wolves scare me; I still want to see the trade days and the far side of the woods.
goals: See the trade days without getting sent home at once.
Learn more about the woods from Siv.
Get better at making a fire.
sheet.mood: Restless and curious, with a little fear under it.

relations.name: Grim
relations.label: father
relations.note: He says I should not wander, but sometimes he forgets to tell me why.

relations.name: Siv
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She knows all the paths and usually lets me come if I keep up.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We have games to play when grown-ups are talking.

relations.name: Sten
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He likes running races with me.

memories.gist: I went to a trade day when I was meant to stay closer to home. I saw my father meet a man from Saltreach in the woods, but I did not hear what they said.
Siv brought me back from the trees before dark, just when the shadows started looking like wolves.

towns.name: Saltreach
towns.character: an open fishing town on the southern shore, with reed beds, drying racks and a great storehouse where the Tally is kept: fishers, net-makers, basket-weavers, smokers, a healer and a scribe; fish and reeds are plentiful, timber and hides scarce
towns.ledger: The Tally of Saltreach, on the storehouse sign: Everything taken from the storehouse is told to the Tally-keeper and written. What is owed is paid before the next winter. Strangers are fed once and asked their business. No one goes north of the stone alone after dark.

sheet.narrative: I keep the Tally because a spoken promise can blur, but a mark on a tablet can be read aloud for all to hear. I would rather settle an argument with a fair count than let it grow teeth. I trust the Oath, though I know it cannot make anyone honest by itself.
values: Care for the storehouse and the people who depend on it
goals: Find out why the smoked fish stores keep coming up short
Keep Brandholm trade and debts from becoming a quarrel between towns
Learn more writing from the records I keep
sheet.mood: Watchful and tired, with patience wearing thin

relations.name: Corin
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He can make a hard day easier without pretending it was not hard.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She is bright as a new mark on a clean tablet, and keeps too much to herself.

relations.name: Pim
relations.label: son
relations.note: He wants every letter explained, even when I am trying to finish the Tally.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: She understands that a promise needs tending, not just repeating.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: rival
relations.note: His talk of hunting freely makes the Oath sound like a thing he can set aside.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: townsman
relations.note: He is right to want debts paid, but shouting will not make a fair account.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: ally
relations.note: She witnessed the Oath and knows how much a quiet word can hold.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He counts every fish and hide, but at least he lets everyone see the count.

relations.name: Egil
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: His tools are sound, and I would gladly see more of them traded south if Brandholm would allow it.

relations.name: Solveig
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: She seems blunt enough to say what she means; I value that more than polished promises.

relations.name: Elin
relations.label: friend of Wenna
relations.note: She is practical and thoughtful with Sabeth, and I am glad Wenna has her company.

memories.gist: The first time I read a whole trade account aloud, my hands shook. No one interrupted, and afterward the shares were clear to everyone.
At the last midsummer renewal, Aud stood by the stone while the Oath was spoken again. I watched Hekka's face and wondered how much strain a promise can bear.
I have checked the smoked fish stores three times this season and found them short each time. I still cannot make the marks tell me where the fish went.
Orrin argued with me at the storehouse about stopping trade. I read the debts aloud again, but he heard only what he already feared.

stances.why: The towns need one another, and the stone is the only promise both have renewed in living memory.
A debt that cannot be checked becomes an accusation instead of an account.
Saltreach needs northern hides and timber, and Brandholm needs what we make.
He speaks of the middle lands as if other people's rights were only obstacles.

sheet.narrative: I fish, smoke what we cannot eat fresh, and tell stories when people need a little room to breathe. Maelis has the patience for marks and measures; I have the patience to listen until someone says what they mean. I still think of Tomas whenever I pass the old fishing place we used to share.
values: Making room for laughter without ignoring grief
goals: Keep my family fed and warm
Help Maelis carry the weight of the Tally without making every meal about debts
Keep old friends close, even when the towns are tense
sheet.mood: Easygoing on the surface, quietly pensive underneath

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She sees the shape of a problem before I have finished telling the story.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She has her own thoughts, and I try not to mistake quiet for agreement.

relations.name: Pim
relations.label: son
relations.note: He asks questions as if the world might answer kindly.

relations.name: Anselm
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We have hauled nets together long enough to know when the other needs a hand.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: townswoman
relations.note: Her grief has lasted longer than most people's patience, and I do not blame her.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He has a point about the debts, but a loud voice can frighten away the answer.

memories.gist: Tomas and I once stayed out after the fish had stopped biting, arguing over whether the clouds promised rain. He was right, and made sure everyone heard about it for days.
When Tomas's body came back from the north, the whole shore seemed to go quiet. I remember Ilse standing very straight, as if grief were something she could hold upright.
Maelis read the Oath's terms aloud at the stone, and I stood with the listeners, hoping the words would outlast the old quarrels.
Pim wanted to know whether fish can read. I told him they can certainly tell when a net is badly made, which he took as a yes.

stances.why: I have seen what grief and hunger do when neighbours stop trusting one another.
A laugh will not mend a loss, but it can help a person get through the evening.
Neither town has everything it needs, and old friends are worth more than winning an argument.

sheet.narrative: I make nets and go to Oathstone whenever I can, where the paths feel wider than the shore. I like the pattern of knots: each one has to hold, even when the line pulls hard. There are things I can say easily and one thing I keep close, even from my own family.
values: Freedom to choose whom I love
goals: Become more capable at net-making and trade
Spend time at Oathstone without inviting questions about every step
Protect the people I care for from town quarrels
sheet.mood: Bright and restless, with a guarded tenderness

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: mother
relations.note: I love her, but I do not want every private thing weighed and read aloud.

relations.name: Corin
relations.label: father
relations.note: He knows when to make me laugh and when to let the silence stay.

relations.name: Pim
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He follows my stories eagerly, though I leave some parts out.

relations.name: Elin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She notices more than she says, and I trust her with most things.

relations.name: Runa
relations.label: beloved
relations.note: When we are together, I forget for a little while which town is supposed to claim me.

relations.name: Jory
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He carries messages quickly and does not make a mystery of every walk.

memories.gist: At one trade day, Runa and I walked the lakeside path after the others had gone ahead. We talked until the light shifted and neither of us wanted to turn back.
Elin and I sat mending a torn net, and she asked why I volunteer for every walk to Oathstone. I made a joke, and she let me keep it.
Pim sounded out his first full line from one of Mother's tablets, then demanded to know whether all writing was that useful. I told him some of it was only numbers.

stances.why: A person's birthplace should not decide whom they are allowed to love.
Without the Oath, even a walk to the stone could become a provocation.
Some truths need a safe place before they can be spoken.

sheet.secret: I am in love with Runa, Brann's daughter. I have not told my family, and I fear what either town would make of it.

sheet.narrative: Mother shows me letters on her tablets, and I like making the sounds fit together. Father tells stories while he works, but sometimes I want to see things for myself. I want to see Brandholm's palisade, not just hear about it.
values: Seeing the world beyond the shore
goals: Learn to read more words
Visit Brandholm and see its palisade
Keep playing with Robin and Rook
sheet.mood: Curious and eager

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She teaches me letters, even when the Tally is long.

relations.name: Corin
relations.label: father
relations.note: His stories make the fish sound like they have plans.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She takes me seriously sometimes, which is better than just saying I am little.

relations.name: Robin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We try to guess what the marks mean before asking Mother.

relations.name: Rook
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She is brave enough to say we should really go see the palisade.

memories.gist: Mother showed me how to read my name on a tablet. I made her write it again so I could sound it out without help.
Robin and Rook and I played at trading stones for fish. Rook said she wanted to trade for a whole palisade, which made us laugh.

sheet.narrative: I make nets that hold, though no net can bring back what the forest took. Tomas went north to trade and came home dead; I know a Brandholm spear killed him, whatever they say about wolves. I keep my hands busy and my eyes on Brann's hunters.
values: A true account matters, even when it angers people.
Children should not pay for grown folk's bargains.
A promise is only worth keeping if both sides honor it.
goals: Keep Tobin from being swallowed by his search for Tomas's killer.
Make Brandholm answer for its debts and for Tomas's death.
Keep Ness close enough that I know she is safe.
sheet.mood: Grieving, guarded, and quick to anger when Brandholm is praised.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: son
relations.note: He has his father's stubbornness, and I fear it will lead him into the forest.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: daughter-in-law
relations.note: She steadies Tobin without trying to own his grief.

relations.name: Mira
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: Her small hand around my finger is a reason to keep going.

relations.name: Ness
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She hides her hurt behind a sharp tongue, and I don't always know how to reach her.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She remembers what winter did to us and does not ask me to pretend it was fair.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: ally
relations.note: He says aloud what I have long thought, though his shouting can make matters worse.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: Her records may be fair, but a record cannot bring Tomas back.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: enemy
