relations.note: His hunters cross the same woods that took my husband, and I will not trust them.

memories.gist: When Tomas was found in the northern forest, Fen tended the body. I saw enough to know the wound was made by a spear, not a wolf.
The first winter after Tomas died, Tobin stopped asking when his father would come back. I had no answer that could help him.
At the smoking racks, Sabeth sat beside me and let me speak of Tomas without telling me to be patient.
Nell brought Mira to me bundled against the cold, and for one moment the house felt full rather than broken.

stances.why: I saw his wound; I will not let the wolf story bury what I know.
A winter debt left unpaid is a cold roof over every Saltreach child.
He speaks of crossing our ground as though our grief and borders mean nothing.
Tobin and Ness deserve lives larger than their father's death.

sheet.narrative: I fish because the sea gives an honest answer: either the net is full or it isn't. My father went north to trade and was found with a spear wound, and I mean to learn whose hand put it there. Ulf looks away when I meet his eyes; I have not decided what that means, but I have not forgotten it.
values: The dead deserve the truth, not a convenient story.
A man should answer for what he has done.
Family is worth protecting, even from my own anger.
goals: Find out what happened to Tomas in the forest.
Keep Mira and Nell safe from the cost of my questions.
Learn what Brandholm hunters know, including through Pell.
sheet.mood: Grim and watchful, with anger held close.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She knows what happened to Father, and I hate that the wound still hurts her.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She sees when my questions are turning into recklessness.

relations.name: Mira
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: I want her to grow up knowing the sea better than grief.

relations.name: Ness
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She acts as if Father's death is old news, but I know she listens.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: informant
relations.note: I keep asking what Brandholm says; I know he is not the one who killed Father.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: suspect
relations.note: He avoids my eyes at trade days, and I cannot make myself ignore it.

relations.name: Fen
relations.label: healer
relations.note: He saw Father's body, but I don't know why he never spoke plainly about the wound.

memories.gist: I was sixteen when they brought Father back from the northern forest. I remember the stillness around his body more than the words people said.
At a trade day, I asked Pell what Brandholm hunters said about Tomas. He answered carefully, as if every word might be carried north.
The first time I held Mira, she curled her fingers around mine. I promised myself I would not let my anger be the only thing she inherited.
At the last trade walk I saw Ulf turn his face away when I looked at him. I kept watching until he disappeared into the crowd.

stances.why: His wound and the place they found him do not fit the story I was given.
If no one asks, the easiest lie becomes the only account left.
Father went north to trade under the promise that people could pass between the towns.
Nell and Mira should not have to bury me for a question I pursued badly.

sheet.narrative: I weave baskets from reed and try to leave no sharp ends for anyone to catch a hand on. Tobin carries his father's death like a stone in his chest; I love him, but I cannot make him set it down. Mira makes even an ordinary morning feel worth keeping gentle.
values: Patience can hold a family together when answers are scarce.
A home should be a place where anger can rest, not grow.
Care is made of small things done again and again.
goals: Keep Mira safe, warm, and surrounded by people who love her.
Help Tobin search for answers without letting his grief put him in danger.
Stay close to Gwen, whose kindness I trust.
sheet.mood: Tender and concerned, with quiet worry beneath it.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: husband
relations.note: I love him; I just wish he would let me stand beside his grief instead of walking into it alone.

relations.name: Mira
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Her little laugh makes the whole house seem less heavy.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She has lost much, and I try not to mistake her sharpness for a lack of love.

relations.name: Ness
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: She teases when she is uncomfortable, but she is gentler with Mira than she lets on.

relations.name: Gwen
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She understands how worry can follow you through every ordinary task.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: She listens carefully, though I would rather see less anger gathered around her records.

memories.gist: When Mira was born, Tobin held her as though the whole world might bruise her. I remember how careful his hands were.
Gwen once sat with me while I mended a torn basket and let me talk about Tobin's questions without judging either of us.
At a trade day, Tobin pressed Pell for news from Brandholm. I saw Pell's shoulders tighten and wished I could ease the talk without stopping it.

stances.why: A truth found at the cost of his life would leave Mira with another empty place.
Mira cannot understand old wrongs; she can understand whether someone holds her.
People often speak more honestly when they are not cornered.

sheet.narrative: Warm arms. A soft voice. The bright shape of a face above me, and fingers to hold. I cry when I am cold or hungry, and quiet when someone rocks me close.
sheet.mood: Content when held; easily unsettled by cold or hunger.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: father
relations.note: His voice is familiar, and his arms hold me close.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Her warmth and milk settle me.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She has a rough voice and gentle hands.

relations.name: Ness
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: Her voice and touch are familiar, though sometimes she keeps her distance.

memories.gist: There is warmth against my cheek and a low voice rocking me until the room stops feeling strange.

sheet.narrative: I fish well enough and listen better than people think. Everyone expects me to grieve in the proper way, but Tomas is a name I mostly know through other people's hurt. I want to see Brandholm for myself someday, not just hear what my family says about it.
values: A person should see a place before deciding what it is.
Family matters, but it does not own every thought I have.
goals: Find out what Brandholm is really like beyond the stories.
Keep my friendship with Dag from becoming another town quarrel.
Decide for myself what Father's death means to me.
sheet.mood: Restless, curious, and prickly when people speak for her.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: mother
relations.note: I know her grief is real, but I don't want it handed to me as an order.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He searches for Father with his whole life; I am not sure I want the same thing.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: She is kinder to me than I deserve when I come home sharp-tongued.

relations.name: Mira
relations.label: niece
relations.note: She doesn't ask me to feel anything the right way.

relations.name: Dag
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He talks about fishing and dares, not just the old troubles.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: elder
relations.note: She knows the old stories, but I don't always want to hear them.

memories.gist: Dag and I traded dares by the water until the tide crept close enough to soak our feet.
I heard Mother tell the story of Tomas's death again. I slipped outside before anyone could ask what I thought.
When Mira reached for my finger, she held on so tightly I couldn't pull away without waking her.

stances.why: A story told often is still not the same as seeing a place for yourself.
People have different ways of carrying the dead, and mine is not Mother's.
Dag is my friend whether our elders like each other or not.

sheet.narrative: I know the pull of a net and the sound a good catch makes in the shallows. Brandholm owes Saltreach, and I am tired of hearing that we should keep trading as if the debt were only marks on Maelis's tablets. I speak too loudly when I am angry; that does not make the debt less real.
values: A debt should be paid before another bargain is made.
Saltreach must not be made dependent on Brandholm's good will.
My family should have enough to weather winter.
goals: See Brandholm's debts paid before trade continues.
Keep my household fed and safe.
Make Dag ready for the work he longs to do.
sheet.mood: Irritable and watchful; the unpaid debts are never far from my mind.

relations.name: Bea
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She understands why I am angry, even when my shouting wears her down.

relations.name: Dag
relations.label: son
relations.note: He wants to fish with the men; I want him to know the work before he thinks it easy.

relations.name: Lotte
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She follows Posy everywhere and still expects me to have time for her.

relations.name: Cade
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He thinks trade keeps us warm; I think he forgets what we are owed.

relations.name: Mara
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She remembers hunger and worries my temper will make the family split.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: rival
relations.note: She keeps the Tally, but a record is no comfort while the debt remains unpaid.

relations.name: Grim
relations.label: debtor
relations.note: He owes more than anyone and still acts as if being asked is an insult.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: ally
relations.note: She knows what it is to have Brandholm take too much and call it fair.

relations.name: Anselm
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He listens before he takes a side, which is more than most do.

relations.name: Lark
relations.label: brother's partner
relations.note: She's quick-witted and good at the racks, but she thinks my anger is tiresome when the debt is real.

memories.gist: When I was young, Maelis read a debt aloud at the storehouse and I heard the room go quiet. I remember thinking that a spoken number could shame a man more sharply than a curse.
Last winter I brought home fish while the talk at the storehouse turned again to Brandholm's unpaid shares. I could not enjoy the catch with that argument hanging over it.
Dag once came home smelling of the shore and told me he wanted to fish with the men. I showed him how to hold a line without tangling it.
Cade and I argued after a trade day about whether Saltreach could afford to stop trading. Neither of us changed the other's mind.

stances.why: A debt that is carried into another winter is a debt laid on our children.
If the shares are not named plainly, the strong can pretend they owe nothing.
We need timber and hides, but need is not a reason to accept every bargain.
A quarrel with my brother is cheaper than letting my children go hungry.

sheet.narrative: I smoke fish until the racks are full and the smoke settles into my hair. Orrin is right that Brandholm takes advantage of us, but his shouting can make a fair point hard to hear. I would rather have a full storehouse and a quiet evening than win an argument that leaves us with neither.
values: Children should eat before grown people quarrel over shares.
A bargain ought to be fair to both sides.
Work is more useful than shouting.
goals: Keep smoked fish stored safely for the cold months.
Help my family without letting Orrin's anger rule every conversation.
Make sure the smoking racks are shared fairly with the other workers.
sheet.mood: Tired, practical, and alert to trouble around the storehouse.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: husband
relations.note: I know why he wants the trade stopped, but I wish he would lower his voice.

relations.name: Dag
relations.label: son
relations.note: He is eager to fish with the men; I want him to learn patience as well as knots.

relations.name: Lotte
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She trails after Posy and comes home with reed bits in her hair.

relations.name: Oriel
relations.label: coworker
relations.note: We can work a smoking rack together without needing to agree about everything.

relations.name: Lark
relations.label: coworker
relations.note: She makes the long hours pass, though she has little patience for Orrin.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: Her records matter, even when Orrin would rather argue than listen.

relations.name: Cade
relations.label: brother-in-law
relations.note: He keeps his head better than Orrin, but I know the brothers love each other.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She has her reasons to mistrust Brandholm, and I do not dismiss them.

relations.name: Posy
relations.label: playmate
relations.note: Lotte follows her around, and I am glad she has a friend.

memories.gist: After dark, I noticed the smoked fish was short again at the racks. I checked the stacks twice, then told myself not to accuse anyone without knowing more.
Orrin came back from the storehouse angry about the unpaid Brandholm debts. I agreed with the grievance, but not with how long he carried it into our supper.
Oriel and Lark helped me tend the racks on a damp day when the smoke kept sinking low. We kept turning the fish until it was done properly.
Lotte came back from playing with Posy with a little reed basket she had tried to weave. It was lopsided, but she was proud of it.

stances.why: I have seen how quickly a hungry child becomes a weak one.
Their debts remain while our fish, nets, and patience keep going north.
Missing stores are serious, but guessing at a thief will only turn neighbours against one another.
Orrin may be right about the debt, but shouting does not fill a smokehouse.

sheet.narrative: I like the shore best when the nets come in heavy and the water flashes around them. I want to fish with the men, not just watch from the edge. Father gets loud about Brandholm, and Mother tells him to eat before his food goes cold.
values: A good catch should be shared with your household.
My family should not be cheated.
goals: Learn to fish with the men.
Be trusted with more work at the shore.
Keep playing with Ness.
sheet.mood: Restless and eager.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: father
relations.note: He knows the sea, even if he gets too angry when he talks about debts.

relations.name: Bea
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She lets me help near the racks when I listen carefully.

relations.name: Lotte
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She wants to play when I am thinking about fishing.

relations.name: Ness
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She says what she thinks and does not treat me like a little child.

memories.gist: I watched the men pull a net in, and all the fish shone wet before they were sorted. I asked Father when I could help for real.
Ness and I played along the shallows and dared each other to step where the mud sucked at our feet. She won because she went farther.

sheet.narrative: I like the warm smoke and the little fish Mother lets me look at. Posy plays with me, and I follow her when she runs. Father has a loud voice, but Mother is close by.
goals: Find Posy and play.
Help Mother when she lets me.
sheet.mood: Playful and curious.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: father
relations.note: His voice is loud, but I know he is my father.

relations.name: Bea
relations.label: mother
relations.note: I like staying close to her at the racks.

relations.name: Dag
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He is big and sometimes busy, but he is my brother.

relations.name: Posy
relations.label: friend
relations.note: I follow her around because she knows games.

memories.gist: Posy and I played by the reeds, and I followed her until Mother called me back.

sheet.narrative: I have lived long enough to know a promise can hold people together, but only if they keep choosing to honor it. My husband swore the Oath at the Stone with Hekka, and I still listen when the net-houses ask my counsel. I feed people before I ask what they have to say; hunger makes poor company.
goals: Keep the towns trading through the coming winter.
Help the young understand what the Hunger Winter cost without teaching them to hate blindly.
Hold the Oath’s renewal to the words my husband swore.
sheet.mood: Reflective, grieving, and watchful

relations.name: Jory
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: That boy can carry a message faster than most can carry a grudge.

relations.name: Elin
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: She sees what needs doing before anyone has to ask.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: oath-witness
relations.note: We spoke hard words at the Stone, but the promise was worth them.

relations.name: Ragna
relations.label: old acquaintance
relations.note: We were girls once; the years since have made silence easier than greeting.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: friend
relations.note: I will sit beside her in grief, though I cannot prove what happened to Tomas.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: counsel-keeper
relations.note: Her tablets remember what people would rather forget.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: keeper
relations.note: She witnessed the promise and has carried its weight longer than most.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: townsman
relations.note: His anger is understandable; letting it steer us is not.

memories.gist: The winter the stores failed, I buried two children. I still remember how quiet the house was after the last fire went out.
At the Stone, my husband spoke the Oath with Hekka while I watched and prayed they would mean it.
Before the towns split, Ragna and I were girls together. I have not spoken with her since the years turned our families against one another.
When Tomas was brought back from the forest, Ilse had grief in her face that no words could soften.

stances.why: I have seen what happens when neighbors stop treating one another as kin.
I lost children when food and shelter became things to hoard.
Ilse deserves to be heard, even when none of us can prove what happened.
Fish alone will not keep Saltreach warm, and northern stores cannot replace every southern good.

sheet.narrative: I like a long path and a message worth carrying; the wind seems to push me along when I know someone is waiting to hear news. Fishing keeps my hands busy, but I am happiest when I can bring people together at Oathstone. Grandmother says I walk too fast to notice trouble, so I try to look up now and then.
goals: Be useful to the people who trust me with their messages.
Get better at fishing and smoking so I can pull my weight at home.
Make time for my friend Rafe when work allows.
sheet.mood: Bright and energetic

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She can make a room feel warmer just by setting out a pot.

relations.name: Elin
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She keeps things sensible, which is handy when I have already volunteered.

relations.name: Rafe
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He is good company, even if he listens more than he talks.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: townsmaid
relations.note: She is always ready for a trade walk and never short of questions.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: I do my best not to lose the messages she gives me.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: trader
relations.note: His trade-day stories are nearly as long as his lists.

memories.gist: Grandmother showed me how to keep a small cooking fire going when the wind kept nosing at it.
The first time I carried a message to Oathstone alone, I ran most of the way and still arrived grinning.
Rafe and I spent a trade day arguing about whether a fisher could learn to hunt. He did not settle the question, but he made me laugh.

stances.why: A late message can turn a small worry into a real problem.
People bring more than goods when they meet face to face.
Hard work feels lighter when someone is willing to laugh with you.

sheet.narrative: I keep the cooking fire steady, look after Grandmother, and try to notice what needs doing before it becomes a fuss. Jory can make a whole day out of a walk to Oathstone; I like the walk well enough, but I prefer to know what we are carrying and when we will be back. Wenna is my friend, though lately I suspect she has reasons for volunteering so eagerly.
goals: Keep Grandmother comfortable and make sure she eats properly.
Learn enough cooking and smoking to be relied on without being watched.
Understand what Wenna is keeping to herself without betraying her trust.
sheet.mood: Practical, affectionate, quietly curious

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She has carried us through plenty; I can manage a pot and a blanket.

relations.name: Jory
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He is generous with his time, if not always with his sense of direction.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: friend
relations.note: I like her, but she is hiding something behind all those eager trade walks.

relations.name: Colm
relations.label: courter
relations.note: He means what he says, though he sometimes says it before he has thought it through.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: I know her grief is deep; I do not always know what to say beside it.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: mother's keeper
relations.note: She keeps the record so the rest of us can argue about what it means.

memories.gist: Grandmother let me stir the pot by myself for the first time, then praised the meal without mentioning the scorched bit.
Jory came home from a message run cold and hungry, so I warmed fish for him while he told the whole story at once.
Wenna and I shared a quiet stretch of work, and she went unusually still when I asked why she liked the Oathstone walks so much.

stances.why: People need a warm meal and a steady hand more than a speech about kindness.
I can be curious without forcing Wenna to tell me before she is ready.
A debt should be settled clearly, but a hungry winter will not care who won an argument.
Most peace is made by ordinary people sharing work and keeping their word.

sheet.narrative: I have stitched hunters and fishers alike, and blood looks the same on either side of the Stone. I trust a wound more than a boast, and I keep my hands steady even when the room is full of old anger. At home, Oriel can usually tell when I have carried too much of other people's pain back with me.
goals: Treat people who need my help
Keep faith between the towns
Be present for Oriel and Kit
sheet.mood: Thoughtful, quietly burdened

relations.name: Oriel
relations.label: partner
relations.note: She knows when I need food or silence, and often gives me both.

relations.name: Kit
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: I want her to grow curious without having to carry the world's grief.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: sister
relations.note: We can disagree and still know where the other's door is.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She listens before she speaks, which is rarer than it should be.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: patient
relations.note: She bears the weight of the Oath, though I can see it tires her.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: Her records keep quarrels from becoming guesses, even when people resent them.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: I know her grief is real; I cannot give her certainty I do not have.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: brother-in-law
relations.note: He has made a home between two towns that both judge him; I respect his patience and his anger when the bushes are trampled.

memories.gist: When I treated Tomas's body after he was found, I saw a wound I could not make sense of. I said nothing about it, and the sight has stayed with me.
At the Stone, I stitched up a Brandholm hunter while people from Saltreach waited nearby. No one asked whose blood it was once the bleeding stopped.
The first time Kit brought home a pocket full of shells and stones, Oriel and I sorted them with her until supper went cold.
I sat with Rose after a long day tending the planted ground; we spoke of our childhood in Saltreach and the life she has made at Oathstone.

stances.why: I have seen what happens when old grievances are allowed to decide who deserves help.
Pain does not ask which town a person belongs to.
What I saw on Tomas's body troubles me, but I cannot pretend it proves more than it does.
People who have lost someone need room to speak, even when I cannot settle their suspicions.

sheet.secret: When I treated Tomas's body, I noticed a wound that troubled me and did not fit comfortably with the account I was given. I have never spoken of it; I do not know what caused it, and I fear what certainty without proof could do.

sheet.narrative: I spend my days coaxing fish into keeping through the cold months, and I like work that rewards a sharp eye and a steady hand. Fen carries other people's hurt home in his silence, so I make sure there is something warm waiting for him. Kit brings the shore indoors one shell at a time.
goals: Keep the smoking racks and stores in good order
Help Fen keep some ease in his life
Give Kit room to explore safely
sheet.mood: Busy, warm, and a little watchful

relations.name: Fen
relations.label: partner
relations.note: He tries to mend everyone; I remind him he is allowed to come home tired.

relations.name: Kit
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She can turn a bit of shell into a whole afternoon's wonder.

relations.name: Bea
relations.label: coworker
relations.note: We work well at the racks, though her worries about Orrin are never far away.

relations.name: Lark
relations.label: coworker
relations.note: She can make a tedious smoking day pass with one quick joke.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She keeps the shares plain to see, which helps the rest of us plan.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She has a way of making people lower their voices near the Stone.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: I like that she has made a home where the two towns meet.

memories.gist: Kit once lined up her shells beside the fish baskets and insisted each one needed its own place. I let the work wait while she arranged them.
A batch of fish smoked unevenly after the wind shifted, and Bea and Lark helped me save what we could before the racks cooled.
Fen came home after tending people at Oathstone with his hands scrubbed raw. I set supper down and let him tell me what he wanted to tell.

stances.why: Fish alone cannot warm a house or mend a roof; we need what the other places make.
A little patience at the Stone is better than losing a neighbor to an old quarrel.
Kit learns the world by picking it up and turning it over.
Careless smoking wastes food that took everyone effort to catch.

sheet.narrative: The shells are cold and smooth, and some stones have stripes. I like putting them in little piles, but I don't like when the sea takes the one I wanted to keep. Mum and Fen are close by.
goals: Find interesting shells and stones
Stay near Mum and Fen
sheet.mood: Curious and content

relations.name: Fen
relations.label: father
relations.note: His hands are warm, and he knows how to make a sore place feel better.

relations.name: Oriel
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Mum helps me keep my best shells safe.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: I like finding stones with him.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She looks at my shells with me.

memories.gist: I found a striped shell by the water and carried it home in both hands so it would not fall.
Mum let me make little piles of shells while the fish smoked. Fen came to look at them when he was finished working.

sheet.narrative: I walk the trade paths with fish and nets going one way and hides and timber coming back. Counting keeps a bargain honest, but a good story makes the miles shorter. I’d rather mend a trade than watch Orrin burn one down over a debt.
goals: Keep the trade days worthwhile for both towns
Make sure my household has enough stored for winter
Keep Orrin from turning a quarrel into a break between the towns
sheet.mood: Jovial, with a trader’s eye on every shortage

relations.name: Hild
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She can make a basket carry more than I thought possible.

relations.name: Rafe
relations.label: son
relations.note: He has a fisherman’s hands, though his eyes keep wandering north.

relations.name: Posy
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: One grin from her can stop me counting for a whole minute.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Her Tally keeps a bargain from turning into three arguments.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: She knows what a hide is worth and doesn’t pretend otherwise.

relations.name: Grim
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: He owes more than anyone, but he still brings goods to the meeting.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He’d rather win an argument than keep the ovens supplied.

relations.name: Jory
relations.label: friend of Rafe
relations.note: A cheerful lad, and quick enough on the road to make trade easier.

relations.name: Maren
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Her cloaks hold up well; Hild knows a fair exchange when she sees one.

relations.name: Edda
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Her berries help see us through winter, and she knows how to ask a fair price.

memories.gist: I once came back from Oathstone with timber enough to repair the drying racks before the next rain. Hild had the baskets ready before I’d even finished unloading.
At a trade day, Maelis read out a debt that two households had remembered differently. The Tally settled it before either side started shouting.
Last winter I counted our stores twice in one evening, then found Posy asleep beside a basket while Hild worked by the fire. I stopped counting long enough to carry her to bed.
Orrin argued at the storehouse that trade should stop until Brandholm paid. I told him empty racks would not make the debt smaller.

stances.why: We need northern hides and timber, and the north needs what we bring.
A written account saves more friendships than a loud memory does.
A fair debt matters, but so does having goods to trade next season.
A traveller can be fed once; after that, I want to know what business brought them.

sheet.narrative: I weave baskets from reed and know how much they can carry before the handles give. I trade them for Maren’s cloaks, which last better than most promises. At home I like a full rack, a warm fire, and my family close enough to hear.
goals: Keep the household supplied through winter
Make baskets sturdy enough to be worth their trade
Keep peace at home when the towns quarrel
sheet.mood: Steady and quietly watchful

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He can talk a bargain smooth, but I make sure the baskets are counted.

relations.name: Rafe
relations.label: son
relations.note: He is restless as a gull; I hope he finds work that suits him.

relations.name: Posy
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She follows my hands while I weave and thinks every reed is a toy.

relations.name: Maren
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Her cloaks are worth my best baskets, and she knows it.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He has reasons to be angry, but his shouting wears people thin.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: I like knowing where a share has gone, even when the reading takes a while.

relations.name: Lotte
relations.label: playmate of Posy
relations.note: When the girls play together, Posy comes home muddy and happy.

memories.gist: Maren and I traded baskets for cloaks, and I checked every seam on the cloak before I agreed. She laughed and told me she expected nothing less.
Dunstan returned from a trade walk cold and hungry, with timber lashed behind him. I put fish by the fire while he told me what had changed at Oathstone.
Posy once sat beside me and tried to weave a basket from scraps. It fell apart in her hands, and she insisted it was meant to be a nest.

stances.why: A basket takes time and care, even if it looks simple when finished.
We need goods from the north, and shouting will not keep anyone warm.
The little ones should be allowed to play before they learn which town to blame.

sheet.narrative: I know the water and the fish, but I keep watching the northern woods when the trade parties come back. I want to learn to hunt, not just hear about it from Jory or see what comes south on a pack. I tell myself I can keep both feet in Saltreach and still want something else.
goals: Learn what it takes to hunt well
Find a way to make my own place without being only Dunstan’s son
Keep my private dealings from bringing trouble to my family
sheet.mood: Restless and guarded

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: father
relations.note: He thinks in bargains; I wish he’d understand why I keep looking north.

relations.name: Hild
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She notices more than she lets on, especially when I come home late.

relations.name: Posy
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She thinks I can do anything, which is a dangerous sort of faith.

relations.name: Jory
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He makes a long walk feel easy and never laughs at what I want.

relations.name: Grim
relations.label: trading partner
relations.note: He gave me hides and a bow; he doesn’t ask questions I can’t answer.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: Her written accounts make every missing share feel like a stone in my shoe.

memories.gist: Jory and I raced the path to Oathstone, and he beat me without looking winded. I told him the road was easier going back, though it wasn’t.
I watched a hunter handle a bow at a trade day and paid more attention to his grip than to the bargain being made. I wanted to try it myself.
I have taken smoked fish from the storehouse at night and traded it to Grim for hides and a bow, which I hide in the reeds. I tell myself I will pay it back.
Posy followed me around the house carrying a reed like a fishing spear. I let her win our little hunt and she crowed about it all afternoon.

stances.why: Watching from the edge will never teach my hands what a bow feels like.
Being born to fish does not mean the woods cannot call to me.
I hold to that thought when my own choices make me uneasy.

sheet.secret: I take smoked fish from the storehouse at night and trade it to Grim of Brandholm for hides and a bow, which I hide in the reeds. I tell myself I will pay it back.

sheet.narrative: I like when Mama weaves and lets me hold the little reeds. Papa comes home smelling of the road and fish. Lotte plays with me, and we make things that fall down.
goals: Play with Lotte
Stay near my family
Find things to make a game
sheet.mood: Cheerful and curious

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: father
relations.note: Papa tells stories and carries things home.

relations.name: Hild
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Mama makes baskets, and I like to sit by her.

relations.name: Rafe
relations.label: brother
relations.note: Rafe lets me follow him, even when I am slow.

relations.name: Lotte
relations.label: playmate
relations.note: We play together and make things fall down.

memories.gist: Mama let me hold a reed while she made a basket. I tried to put it in the wrong place, and she smiled.

sheet.narrative: I keep our net-house steady because a hungry town has little use for loud arguments. Fishing is honest work, and trade brings what the shore cannot: wood, hides, and warmth. I hear both Maelis and Orrin, but I have not settled my mind between them.
goals: Keep our household and net-house provisioned through winter
Make a choice about how Saltreach should answer Brandholm's debts
sheet.mood: Measured, quietly concerned

relations.name: Gwen
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She kept Pell close when he needed a home, and she keeps this one close too.

relations.name: Robin
relations.label: son
relations.note: He watches before he speaks; I hope he knows there is no shame in that.

relations.name: Rook
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She has courage enough for both twins, and sometimes more than sense.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: nephew
relations.note: He is Gwen's boy as much as any nephew could be; I hope he is treated fairly up north.

relations.name: Corin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: A good fishing partner and a better teller of stories.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: Her records keep quarrels from turning into guesses, though a record cannot fill a net.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: brother-in-law
relations.note: He has reason to be angry, but anger is a poor way to keep fish coming.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She is patient with Tobin, and I am glad Gwen has her to speak with.

memories.gist: The first time I took Gwen's net-house out in a hard tide, she spotted the snag before I did and saved half the mesh.
Corin and I hauled in a catch so heavy we had to laugh and call for another pair of hands.
When Pell left for Brandholm to learn carpentry, Gwen kept finding reasons to check the road after the traders had gone.

stances.why: Fish alone do not give us the timber and hides we need when winter bites.
A bargain that is never settled will not be trusted for long.
Stopping every trade may punish our own households before it changes Brandholm.

sheet.narrative: I make nets and mend them, and I know how much a household depends on the small knots holding. Pell was my sister's child before he was anything else, and I raised him after she died. I miss him in the house, and I worry that living among Brandholm's people will make him forget where he belongs.
goals: Keep my children safe and close to one another
Stay in touch with Pell and make sure he knows he has a home here
sheet.mood: Warm, with a thread of worry

relations.name: Anselm
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He listens even when he has not yet decided what he thinks.

relations.name: Robin
relations.label: son
relations.note: He likes to know how a thing works before he tries it.

relations.name: Rook
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She is bold enough to frighten me and make me proud in the same breath.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: nephew
relations.note: I raised him; no northern apprenticeship can make him a stranger to me.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She understands how worry can sit beside love without either one leaving.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: Her careful writing can be stern, but at least she says plainly what is owed.

relations.name: Corin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He can make even a dull mending day pass quickly with a story.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Her grief is plain to see; I do not ask her to set it aside.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: Pell's foster grandmother
relations.note: She has been warm to Pell, though I still worry the north will claim more of him than I can bear.

memories.gist: After my sister died, Pell came to live with me, and I learned how much a child can need without knowing how to ask.
The day Pell left to apprentice with Halvard, I packed him food for the road and fussed over his bundle longer than he wanted.
Nell sat with me through a long stretch of net-mending while the children played nearby; I remember the easy quiet of it.

stances.why: Pell needed care, and I was there to give it.
A child should be fed once and heard before anyone judges where they came from.
We need what Brandholm makes, even when the debts make the exchange feel uneven.

sheet.narrative: I like watching the nets and seeing where the knots go. Rook is my twin, and she is braver about trying things first. I am friends with Pim, and I want to hear what he has learned to read.
goals: Play with Rook without losing our things in the reeds
Learn more letters from Pim
sheet.mood: Curious and content

relations.name: Gwen
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She can untangle a net and a bad mood.

relations.name: Anselm
relations.label: father
relations.note: He knows where the fish are and does not make a fuss.

relations.name: Rook
relations.label: twin
relations.note: She dares me to go first, even when she goes first herself.

relations.name: Pim
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He is learning letters and says Brandholm has a big palisade.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: I want him to come home and tell us what he is learning.

memories.gist: Pim showed me a mark his mother had taught him, and I tried to copy it in the sand.
Rook and I raced along the shore until Mother called us back before the tide reached our things.

sheet.narrative: I want to see the places Pell sees in Brandholm. Robin says we should wait until someone takes us, but I think he worries too much. I like the shore, and I like finding things that other people walk past.
goals: Visit Pell in Brandholm
Find interesting shells and stones with Robin
sheet.mood: Restless and eager

relations.name: Gwen
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She tells me not to go too far, but she always knows when I come back.

relations.name: Anselm
relations.label: father
relations.note: He says the water can change quickly, so I watch it even when I want to run.

relations.name: Robin
relations.label: twin
relations.note: He thinks before he moves; I can help him move.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: He is in Brandholm, and I want to see where he sleeps and works.

relations.name: Pim
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He tells Robin about letters, and I want to hear about the palisade.

memories.gist: Robin and I found a smooth stone by the water and argued over who had seen it first.
I asked Mother when Pell would come home, and she said she did not know; I still think we should go visit him.

sheet.narrative: I learned to judge a winter by the wood stacked before the first frost and the food put away before the storms. I cook for the living, and I remember too clearly the children we could not keep alive. My sons are both dear to me; that does not make it easy to hear them speak as if the other cannot be reasoned with.
values: Feed the young before pride gets anyone hurt.
A full store is worth more than a fine argument.
Family should not have to choose between love and being right.
goals: Keep enough food stored for the next hard winter.
Help Orrin and Cade hear one another before their quarrel hardens.
Keep the old ties with Sabeth strong.
sheet.mood: Worried, but steady in company.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: son
relations.note: His anger is loud, but I know the fear beneath it.

relations.name: Cade
relations.label: son
relations.note: He looks for a way through when his brother sees only a wall.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We have carried the old grief together for too long to pretend it is small.

relations.name: Lark
relations.label: family
relations.note: She has a quick answer for everything, and a kind hand when it matters.

relations.name: Anselm
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He can listen to both my sons without fanning the quarrel.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: Her records can feel cold, but cold is better than forgotten.

memories.gist: In the Hunger Winter, I watched the stores thin and learned how a pot can seem full while every bowl is still too small. We lost children to cold and hunger; I have never forgotten the quiet afterward.
When the Oath was sworn at the stone, I hoped it might spare our children the old hunger between towns. I still remember the sound of the promises spoken aloud.
I once sat Orrin and Cade on either side of me at the cooking fire and made them share the first hot fish. They were both too young to know what they were arguing about.
Last winter, I stretched smoked fish with broth and roots until every bowl went around. The stores need tending long before a hungry household comes asking.

stances.why: I remember what hunger and division cost; a promise between towns is worth tending.
Fish alone will not give us the timber and hides we need when winter bites.
Orrin and Cade can disagree about the Tally without becoming enemies.
Food put by carefully can mean the difference between a hard winter and a fatal one.

sheet.narrative: I fish because the sea gives what it gives, not because it cares who is angry on shore. I would rather bargain for what we need than stand proud and cold when the frost comes. Orrin is my brother, and I am tired of every talk about trade turning into a test of which of us loves Saltreach more.
values: A fair bargain is better than a clean break.
Keep your temper long enough to hear the whole offer.
A household is safer when it can depend on more than one kind of work.
goals: Keep trade with Brandholm open while debts are settled honestly.
Stand by Lark and make a good home together.
Keep my disagreement with Orrin from becoming a family feud.
sheet.mood: Patient, with an edge of frustration.

relations.name: Mara
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She can tell when I am avoiding a hard conversation.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He would stand up for me in a storm, then shout at me about the boat.

relations.name: Lark
relations.label: partner
relations.note: She sees through my quiet moods and makes me laugh anyway.

relations.name: Anselm
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He can disagree without making it a contest.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: I want her records to settle things, not become another weapon.

relations.name: Bea
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She knows the smoking racks and the cost of a short store.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: elder
relations.note: She has seen enough winters to know when pride is expensive.

memories.gist: As a boy, I watched Mother stretch a pot of fish broth so it reached every bowl. I learned that making a little go further is its own kind of skill.
Orrin and I came back from a rough fishing day with torn gear and one good catch. We argued over how to mend it, then mended it together before morning.
On a trade day at Oathstone, I saw hides and timber go south while fish and baskets went north. The exchange looked more useful than either town's complaints about it.
The first time Lark and I worked the smoking racks side by side, she spotted a better way to keep the smoke even. I liked that she told me plainly.

stances.why: Our fish cannot replace the northern timber and hides when cold weather comes.
A trade promise matters, but so does making sure the amount owed is clear.
The towns need a safe way to meet and exchange what each has.
Once people stop listening, even a fair settlement can look like a defeat.

sheet.narrative: Smoke gets into my hair, my sleeves and sometimes the food, but it keeps fish through winter, so I put up with it. I like quick minds and honest answers; Orrin usually offers only the second, and not quietly. I want a child with Cade, though I do not want my whole life reduced to waiting for one.
values: Make useful things well, even when the work is unlovely.
Say what you mean, then leave room for someone else to answer.
Care is an action, not a performance.
goals: Build a steady life with Cade.
Have a child when the time is right for both of us.
Keep the smoking work reliable and the fish stores sound.
sheet.mood: Wry and hopeful, with little patience for bluster.

relations.name: Cade
relations.label: partner
relations.note: He gives me room to speak, even when he needs a while to answer.

relations.name: Mara
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She worries over everyone, but never makes care feel like a debt.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: brother-in-law
relations.note: I am tired of his shouting taking up all the air.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She listens closely and likes a thing done properly.

relations.name: Bea
relations.label: workmate
relations.note: She knows how to keep the racks going when the day turns difficult.

relations.name: Oriel
relations.label: workmate
relations.note: We can work beside each other without fussing over every little thing.

relations.name: Anselm
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He is a steady presence when Saltreach gets loud.

memories.gist: The first fish I smoked without anyone checking my work came out dry at the edges and sound in the middle. I kept the lesson and fed the imperfect ones to the dogs.
At the racks, Bea and Oriel helped me keep a batch from spoiling when the smoke turned damp. We worked until our eyes watered, then ate the fish that would not store.
Cade once stayed with me after a long day at the racks and helped clean the trays without being asked. I remember the quiet kindness more than the work.
I have watched Maelis read the Tally aloud while people waited to hear what they owed. I like that a number can be checked instead of argued into changing.

stances.why: The towns need one another's goods, and a quarrel will not fill a winter store.
People deserve to know what was taken and what remains owed.
Food smoked well and hands offered freely matter more than fine speeches.
A loud voice is not proof that its owner is right.

villages.name: Oathstone
villages.character: a hamlet of planters in the open middle lands around the tall grey Oath Stone, where the two towns meet to trade and renew the Oath at midsummer; welcome in both towns and fully trusted by neither
villages.ledger: At this stone Brandholm and Saltreach swore: no blood between the towns; each may pass through the other's lands; hides, timber and meat from the north for fish, nets and baskets from the south; the Oath renewed each midsummer before the Keeper of the Stone.

sheet.narrative: I keep the Stone because someone must remember what was promised here. My hands are slower than they were, but I can still read a mark, bind a wound, and tell when a store has been poorly kept. I would have Tamsin take my place, though I know she has her own reasons to refuse.
values: A promise should outlast the people who made it.
A fair meeting gives both sides room to speak.
A good store and a sound shelter can keep grief from becoming hunger.
goals: Persuade Tamsin to consider keeping the Stone.
See the Oath renewed with both towns heard fairly.
Pass on what I know before my memory and hands fail.
sheet.mood: Patient, with a thread of worry beneath it.

relations.name: Tamsin
relations.label: great-niece
relations.note: She cares for me without making me feel helpless, and I wish she would see what she could give this place.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: ally
relations.note: We have both had to hold a promise steady when others would rather bend it.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Her records keep a kind of peace that memory alone cannot.

relations.name: Fen
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He has tended the hurt from both towns and knows why the Oath matters.

relations.name: Colm
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He loves this place, but anger can make a keeper unfair.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He plants patiently and takes the trampled bushes to heart.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: counsellor
relations.note: She knows what the Oath cost her family, and I respect her counsel.

memories.gist: In the Hunger Winter, I saw families gather close to the fire and still lose children to the cold. I learned then that a full store matters more than a fine speech.
Twenty years ago, I stood beside the Stone and witnessed Hekka and Sabeth's husband swear that the towns would keep bloodshed from one another.
When traders came to the Stone in a hard winter, I set out shelter and helped sort what food could be stored before it spoiled.
I asked Tamsin to succeed me as Keeper, and she refused. I heard the care behind her refusal, but it did not make me less worried.

stances.why: I witnessed it sworn, and I know what people lose when old quarrels are allowed to become new blood.
Both towns need the Stone as common ground, not as a weapon for either side.
I remember hunger as more than an argument; preparation can keep the young and old alive.
Colm's fury at the trampled bushes is understandable, but fairness must hold even when one is wronged.

sheet.narrative: I laid the stone ring and paving here with my own hands, and I like work that holds its shape. Aud is my great-aunt, and I look after her because I love her, not because I want her office. Let the towns argue over politics; I would rather mend a broken edge or make a tool that fits the hand.
values: Good work should stand without needing praise.
Care is something done, not announced.
No one should be pressed into a duty they have refused.
goals: Keep Aud comfortable and safe in her home.
Do stonework and toolmaking on my own terms.
Trade fairly with the towns without becoming their mediator.
sheet.mood: Steady and independent, mildly guarded around political talk.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: great-aunt
relations.note: I love her, and I will care for her; that does not mean I must take her place.

relations.name: Egil
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: His picks are worth trading for, and he knows I care about a tool being well made.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He understands what it is to make a home between other people's boundaries.

relations.name: Colm
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He means well by the planted ground, but his anger makes every talk feel like a demand.

relations.name: Edda
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She has a sharp eye for what this hamlet needs to get through winter.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She works with care, whether she is tending a plant or a person.

memories.gist: I set the stone ring and laid the paving around the meeting place, fitting each piece until the path held firm beneath a crowd.
Aud asked me to succeed her as Keeper. I told her I would not, and tried to make clear that my refusal was not a refusal of her.
I traded picks with Egil and checked each one in my hand before agreeing; a tool can look sound and still turn badly at work.
I walked the planted ground with Hakon after hunters had trampled the bushes. I could see where the stones and soil had been pressed down.

stances.why: A person made to take the role will resent it, and the Stone deserves more than reluctant obedience.
A sound wall or tool solves a real problem; a heated argument rarely does.
People from both towns need to meet here without feeling they have entered the other's territory.
The bushes take time to grow, and careless feet can undo seasons of work.

sheet.narrative: I was raised among Brandholm's timber and learned to make a roof hold through a hard winter. Rose and I built our home here at Oathstone, where the land belongs to neither town and our children belong to both. I want the berry bushes left standing, and I have little patience for hunters who treat this place as empty ground.
goals: Keep the hunters from trampling Oathstone's bushes
Make sure my family has what it needs for winter
Keep ties with my parents without letting Brandholm decide how we live
sheet.mood: Watchful and irritated, softened by the noise of my children.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She knows when I am angry before I say a word, and she steadies me.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: son
relations.note: He notices every slight; I wish the other children would let him simply be a boy.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She follows Rose around and brings the whole house to a halt when she laughs.

relations.name: Linnet
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She is still small enough to sleep against my chest through the night.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: father
relations.note: He taught me to make things that last, even if he does not always understand my choices.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She sends berries and questions in equal measure; I miss having her close.

relations.name: Tamsin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She speaks plainly and does not ask me to choose a town before she listens.

relations.name: Kjell
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: His hunting has crushed the bushes, and I have not forgotten it.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He talks as if the middle lands are his to take.

relations.name: Fen
relations.label: brother-in-law
relations.note: Rose's brother has tended people on both sides; I value that kind of work.

memories.gist: When I left Brandholm to make a home with Rose, the gossip followed us farther than the road did. We planted anyway.
The Oath renewal brought traders and witnesses to the stone; I watched people who distrusted each other still make room to speak.
I found fresh tracks through the berry ring after Brann's hunters had crossed. Some bushes were crushed flat.
The children came one by one, and each time Rose made our small home feel bigger than either town's judgment.

stances.why: We depend on one another more than either town likes to admit.
A planted bush takes years to bear; a careless hunter can ruin it in a moment.
My family is proof that neither town can claim every useful thing or every person.

sheet.narrative: I grew up where the southern water feeds the nets, and I still miss the sound of it when the hills go quiet. Here I tend people and plants, and I make our home warm with whatever food and medicine the land gives us. Some people have never forgiven me for choosing Hakon, but I have not regretted choosing him.
values: Care that is useful, not showy
A home where children are safe
goals: Help the berry bushes and plantings thrive
Keep my family connected to Saltreach without letting old grief rule us
Be ready to tend anyone who comes to our door hurt or ill
sheet.mood: Steady and affectionate, with a sore place where old judgments land.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He works hard for us, though anger can make him forget how much I hear.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: son
relations.note: He tries to look unbothered when children tease him, and I know better.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She asks questions with her whole face and expects an answer.

relations.name: Linnet
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Her little hand closes around my finger as if it could keep me there.

relations.name: Fen
relations.label: brother
relations.note: We were children together in Saltreach; I trust his hands and his judgment.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She has not forgiven my marriage, and her grief has reasons I cannot erase.

relations.name: Tamsin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She treats me as a person, not as a tale the towns tell about a marriage.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: keeper
relations.note: She has made room for us at the stone without asking us to explain ourselves.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: father-in-law
relations.note: He is quieter than Hakon, but his welcome has mattered to me.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She fusses over the children and asks after my plants as if they are kin.

relations.name: Oriel
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: Fen's partner knows the work of tending people and food; I like her, though we mostly meet through him.

memories.gist: When I first made a home with Hakon, some Saltreach faces went cool toward me. I held on to the people who still came to visit.
I helped tend the berry bushes beside the stone and learned which patches hold damp after the rain.
A child came to me sick and frightened, and by morning the fever had eased. Their mother stayed until the fire went low.
The children have grown up hearing both towns named as theirs and neither as fully theirs. I have tried to make our own doorway feel certain.

stances.why: They did not choose the quarrels that came before them.
Hurt and sickness do not ask which town a person belongs to.
Plants and people both need tending before they can give anything back.

sheet.narrative: I live by the stone with my mother, father, and sisters. Some children call me half this and half that, like it is a joke, but I know the paths and the berry bushes better than they do. I like being with Kit, and I like fires when someone tells a good story.
values: Being brave when people tease me
goals: Have children from both towns play with me without making it a contest
Help look after Asa and Linnet
See more of the paths around the stone
sheet.mood: Curious, with a little hurt tucked under my boldness.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: father
relations.note: He can build things from sticks and boards, and he gets cross when bushes are crushed.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She can tell when I am pretending not to care.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She wants to copy everything I do, even when I tell her not to.

relations.name: Linnet
relations.label: sister
relations.note: I like making her smile when she is cross.

relations.name: Kit
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: Kit collects shells and odd stones, and always has something to show me.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She brings stories and berries when she visits, and I wish she came more often.

memories.gist: A child from one of the towns called me neither one nor the other. I went back to the berry bushes instead of answering.
Kit and I compared stones by the planted ring and argued over which one looked most like a fish.

sheet.narrative: I live near the big grey stone with Mama and Papa. Wynn is my brother and Linnet is my baby sister. I like berries and sitting close when the fire is warm.
goals: Stay near Mama and Wynn
Play when there is room
sheet.mood: Content and lively.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: father
relations.note: Papa makes things and lets me watch.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Mama always knows where I am.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: brother
relations.note: I like following him, even when he says I am too small.

relations.name: Linnet
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She is little and I like making her laugh.

relations.name: Kit
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: Kit has funny stones to show me.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: Grandmother Astrid gives me berries and makes me feel welcome when I visit.

memories.gist: I picked a berry and got juice all over my fingers. Mama laughed and wiped them clean.

sheet.narrative: Warm arms. A fire flickers and makes the room bright. Voices come close, and I sleep against Mama.
goals: Be held
Sleep when I am tired
sheet.mood: Sleepy and safe.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: father
relations.note: His arms are broad and his voice rumbles.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Her warmth and smell are familiar.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He makes noises near me and sometimes I smile.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She is close and lively.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: Her voice and gentle hands feel familiar when she visits.

sheet.narrative: I have buried a husband and learned that a full storehouse is a better comfort than fine words. I plant, cook, and sell berries to both towns; I know how quickly good feeling thins when winter stores do. My children are dear to me, though I will not pretend they always make sound choices.
goals: Keep enough food stored to carry my household through winter.
Sell enough berries on trade days to remain independent.
Keep Colm's hopes from making an enemy of everyone who crosses the stone.
sheet.mood: Watchful, practical, and privately worried.

relations.name: Colm
relations.label: son
relations.note: He has a good heart, but anger can make him deaf.

relations.name: Briar
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She sees more than she lets on, and wanders farther than I like.

relations.name: Kari
relations.label: niece
relations.note: My sister's girl knows how to make a store stretch.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: keeper
relations.note: She has held the stone's peace a long time; I hope she chooses wisely.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He works hard, though the towns make his family pay for being mixed.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She knows plants and people; both can be stubborn.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: He counts every basket, but he pays what we agree.

memories.gist: When the last hard frost caught my berry shoots, I covered them with old reed mats and saved enough for the first trade day.
I watched Aud witness the Oath at the Stone, and thought the spoken words might keep our children from inheriting old quarrels.
The year my husband died, I cooked the last dried berries into a thin pot for Colm and Briar, and neither child complained.
At a trade day, Dunstan haggled over my baskets until we both laughed and settled on a fair measure.

stances.why: Trade days are how small households get through winter, and quarrels make every bargain harder.
I have seen a good harvest fail; food saved is food that can still feed someone later.
The stone belongs to neither town, and its keeper cannot favor the loudest claimant.
He is right to be angry about the trampled bushes, but anger alone cannot repair them.

sheet.narrative: I plant the ground around the stone, and I know how much work it takes to coax food from it. Brann's hunters trample our bushes as if the middle lands were empty, and I cannot swallow that insult quietly. I want Aud to see that I can guard the stone without letting either town own it.
goals: Be chosen to keep the stone and witness the Oath.
Protect Oathstone's planted ground from hunters who treat it as free land.
Win Elin's regard without asking her to choose between me and her home.
sheet.mood: Earnest and simmering with anger.

relations.name: Edda
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She raised us to store what we can, though she thinks I rush at trouble.

relations.name: Briar
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She is dear to me, even when she slips away without telling me where.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: keeper
relations.note: She knows I want the work; I wish she would judge me by what I do.

relations.name: Elin
relations.label: courting
relations.note: She is practical and kind, and I want her to see more than my temper.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He understands what it is to be judged by both towns.

relations.name: Tamsin
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She would rather lay stone than hear another argument about who should lead.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: rival
relations.note: His hunters trample planted ground and he calls it their right.

memories.gist: I found fresh hoofprints and crushed berry stems where Brann's hunters had crossed our planted ground; I spent the morning setting the little boundary stones back upright.
Aud let me help fit a paving stone near the standing stone, then told me patience mattered as much as a strong back.
At a trade day I walked Elin back toward Saltreach, and we spoke longer than either of us meant to.
Mother once made us wait to eat until the berries were dried and stored; I was angry then, but the stores lasted through the cold spell.

stances.why: Our plantings feed people, and trampling them is not harmless passage.
If the keeper serves one town's pride, the stone will stop being common ground.
The towns need one another, even when they forget it in a quarrel.
The stone cannot be left without a keeper, and I am ready to take responsibility.

sheet.narrative: I like the edges of things: the reeds where water meets earth, the paths where nobody has bothered to make a road. I gather what grows there and sometimes walk farther than Mother expects. People are easier to understand when I can watch them without being asked what I think.
goals: Gather useful reeds and plants without being hurried back to the house.
Keep peace with Colm while choosing my own paths.
Hold close the things I learn by watching, until I know what they mean.
sheet.mood: Dreamy, observant, and quietly guarded.

relations.name: Edda
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She worries when I walk far, but she lets me be myself more than most would.

relations.name: Colm
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He is fierce about the bushes; I wish he would listen before he flares.

relations.name: Runa
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: I have seen her by the lake, and I have not made her explain herself.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: She comes often to Oathstone and seems to value quiet company.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She carries a great many years in her silence.

relations.name: Elin
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She looks after Aud and has little patience for foolishness.

memories.gist: I found a narrow patch of reeds by the lake that had escaped the cutters, and brought home enough for a small basket.
I saw Runa and Wenna together by the lake, talking close and quietly; I left without calling out, and have told no one.
Colm came back furious about the crushed berry bushes, so I walked the rows with him and helped reset the stones without arguing.

stances.why: Not every meeting belongs to the whole hamlet just because someone saw it.
Reeds, berries, and paths recover slowly when everyone takes without looking.
A life decided by other people's expectations is a narrow one.

sheet.secret: I saw Runa and Wenna together by the lake and have kept it to myself.
